articles.title: 8 people arrested after Abu Dhabi hotel brawl; Usman Nurmagomedov barred from RAF event
articles.summary: Abu Dhabi police say they have arrested eight people following a hotel brawl involving Merab Dvalishvili and Usman Nurmagomedov.
articles.body:
Abu Dhabi police say they have arrested eight people in response to the hotel brawl involving former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, among others.

Video of the incident emerged online Wednesday , along with a video message showing a bloodied Dvalishvili claiming he was attacked from behind by Nurmagomedov and several other men.

According to a social media post by Abu Dhabi police , eight people were later arrested, including those who filmed the incident.

"The General Command of Abu Dhabi Police was able to arrest 8 persons involved in a fight that took place at the entrance of a hotel, on the background of previous differences between them, they also managed to arrest two persons who filmed the incident, take the necessary legal actions on their right, and refer them to the General Prosecutor to complete the proceedings in accordance with the laws enacted by it," said a statement posted to the official Instagram account of the Abu Dhabi police.

"The details of the incident go back to a fight at the entrance of a hotel, following previous differences between a number of people, and immediately, the Abu Dhabi Police specialized teams initiated their actions to deal with the incident, and they were able to arrest those involved, as well as arresting the two persons who filmed the fight, and taking the necessary legal actions for their rights," the statement continued.

"Abu Dhabi police stressed its keenness to maintain public security and order, and deal firmly with behaviors that would violate security or endanger the safety of others, stressing the importance of adhering to laws and regulations and civilized and responsible behavior."

The incident has also thrown into question the lineup for Saturday's RAF Abu Dhabi wrestling event. Dvalishvili is in Abu Dhabi to wrestle former WSOF bantamweight champion Marlon Moraes at Saturday's event. UFC bantamweight Umar Nurmagomedov — the brother of Usman Nurmagomedov, who could be seen slapping Dvalishvili at the start of the hotel brawl — is also slated to wrestle UFC Hall of Famer Urijah Faber at the same event.

Neither fighter was present at Thursday's RAF press conference, according to MMA Fighting , and RAF co-founder Chad Bronstein said he did not yet know the status of those matches. Bronstein did say that, regardless of whether the matches move forward, Usman Nurmagomedov would not be welcome at the event.

"We're hoping that the situation gets resolved, sooner than later," Bronstein said on Thursday. "And obviously, Usman will not be attending our event on Saturday night."

The brawl involving Dvalishvili and the Nurmagomedov brothers comes after months of hostility between the two camps. Dvalishvili defeated the elder brother, Umar, in a UFC bantamweight title clash early last year. The two sides have engaged in a war of words ever since, though this week's incident was the most consequential clash yet, leaving several people visibly bruised and bloodied.

articles.title: El 'cambio' de Joel Álvarez: "Aunque suene mal, antes me daba igual morir allí"
articles.standfirst: El peleador español ha analizado su situación en la UFC y el cambio de perspectiva que ha tenido desde que ha sido padre
articles.summary: El peleador español ha analizado su situación en la UFC y el cambio de perspectiva que ha tenido desde que ha sido padre
articles.body: Joel Álvarez ha vuelto a aparecer públicamente para hablar de cómo ha cambiado su perspectiva como peleador desde que ha sido padre y ha formado una familia. En sus últimos dos combates en la UFC, 'El Fenómeno' ha sufrido dos duras derrotas ante Yaroslav Amosov y Chidi Njokuani, y en una entrevista con Eurosport ha analizado en qué punto de su carrera se encuentra ahora mismo y cuáles son sus planes para el futuro. En su combate contra Amosov el pasado mayo, Joel fue sometido por un peleador candidato a ir por el cinturón en un futuro no muy lejano, pero ante Njokuani sí que dejó una imagen más preocupante. No parecía el mismo, aunque también hay que aclarar que aceptó el combate en corto aviso después de que se lesionase el rival original de Chidi, pero no salió a finalizar como sí pasaba antes. De hecho, el peleador gijonés ha reconocido que ha cambiado, ya que ahora es una persona totalmente diferente. "Puedo decirte que he vuelto más frío y calculador en la jaula, no tan emotivo. Antes era más a lo que saliese. Me daba igual morir allí. Solamente tenía perro, que era lo que me hacía volver, y ahora tengo una familia, morir es lo último que quiero. Ese Joel sanguinario que era antes ha cambiado, se ha recogido un poco", sentenció. Otra cosa en la que incidió tras su última derrota es que necesitaba tiempo para sanar la cabeza, ya que jamás había perdido dos combates en su carrera. A día de hoy tendrá que volver a ganarse su puesto para acercarse al top 15 de peso wélter, pero antes buscará reencontrarse consigo mismo. "Me ha afectado perder dos combates seguidos y necesito recuperarme", finalizó. Por tanto, no se espera que 'El Fenómeno' regrese hasta el segundo trimestre de 2027, una vez sus heridas tanto físicas como mentales sanen, ya que viene de operarse de una hernia y de sufrir una lesión en la mano en su combate contra Njokuani. Hay nombres que le interesan como el de Daniel Rodríguez, pero deberá sentarse con la UFC y hablar cuando llegue el momento para ver que le ofrecen de cara a superar este pequeño bache y volver a ser ese finalizador nato que era el terror de peso ligero. Seguramente veamos un Joel Álvarez 2.0 tras escuchar esta entrevista, pero eso no quiere decir que el objetivo haya cambiado. 'El Fenómeno' sigue vigente, y ahora su deber es demostrarlo en el octágono.

articles.title: Gerome Warburton: Welsh boxer out to prove he is world-level against Carlos Adames
articles.summary: Welsh boxer Gerome Warburton plans to show the world he is a top contender in the middleweight division when he faces WBC champion Carlos Adames.
articles.body:
Welsh boxer Gerome Warburton says facing world champion Carlos Adames will complete his boxing journey as he looks to prove he belongs at the top level.

The 31-year-old will face WBC middleweight champion Adames, 32, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday, 14 November, though the world title is not on the line.

The WBA continental champion is not ranked by the WBC, and will instead face once-beaten Adames at super-middleweight in a non-title main event.

Warburton, from Colwyn Bay, believes he has earned this career-defining shot after years of overcoming the odds on the British scene.

"You're in there to do a job. Yes, he's a world champion, but this is my time to show the world that I belong at this level," Warburton told BBC Sport.

"All of my hard work has got me here. This is a big hurdle to get over, but I've been jumping over hurdles my whole career."

The 5ft 11in (1.8m) former Welsh middleweight champion added: "This is another occasion to prove wrong those people who think I can't achieve something. I don't feel any pressure - the pressure is all on him.

"He's the WBC champion. He's the one who has set out to put on a show-stopping performance as world champ. I'm going there to upset the apple cart."

Workaholic with a tattooed throat – meet The Merthyr Mexican

Price rules out Shields but hints at big showdown

Headlining Zuffa Boxing's first show in Saudi Arabia will mark a new high point in a "crazy" rise for Warburton, who never set out to become a world champion.

He faces a quick turnaround, too, having beaten veteran Englishman Nathan Heaney to retain his WBA continental middleweight title on 26 September.

Consecutive victories over former British champion Heaney have given Warburton's career fresh momentum, exceeding even his own expectations.

"I never thought that beating Nathan Heaney twice would have gotten me where I am now. I took the risk to face him twice, and it's brought a reward," Warburton said.

Initially, Warburton had his eyes on the Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury undercard in Cardiff before landing a fight that he thought was a joke when first informed.

"I was back in the gym training full time and had a phone call from my manager telling me they had asked Zuffa if I could face a certain boxer," Warburton recalled.

"They came back and said no, but that I could face Carlos Adames. I was taken aback and thought, 'Are you telling me lies? Is this true?'

"After a split second, it hit me that I had finally got a good reward for all of my hard work, and then he dropped the news that it wouldn't be for his WBC title.

"As they say in boxing, things happen quickly. Beat Carlos Adames and I could be on the road for the WBC world title."

Wales has a rich history of world champion boxers, but none of the 14 men and women who have claimed top honours in the sport hail from north Wales.

Barmouth-born Johnny Williams held the British and Empire heavyweight titles, but he received his boxing education after moving to English town Rugby at age three.

Warburton now has the chance to become north Wales' most celebrated boxer, as he prepares to become the first from the region to face a world champion.

"I feel as though I don't get the recognition for doing that," he added.

"I'm holding the flag for north Wales. If I could get my hands on a world title, or box for one, it would be a dream come true, and I'd be writing history."

Warburton, who goes by the moniker 'The Breadmaker', will not be joined by family for the trip to Saudi Arabia, but knows they will be watching back home.

While son Roman was present for both fights against Heaney and celebrated in the ring, Warburton prefers to "zone in" when fighting further afield.

"Unfortunately, I've banned all of my family members from going over because I treat boxing like work," Warburton explained.

"My family come when I fight closer to home, but when I'm away, I like to be on my own with my team. They wouldn't come to work with me.

"I have to be zoned in, and I know that everyone will be watching from home. One of my friends is coming because he likes to be adventurous."

Warburton expects the Riyadh crowd to be behind Adames and believes that will play into his hands, as it has done throughout his career.

"I'm used to not having the crowd [behind me] and having them boo me. The two Heaney fights showed that," he said.

"I could go into the lion's den, and it still wouldn't bother me."

Beyond the boxing accolades, Warburton knows how much an upset victory over Adames would change his family's life.

"Win this and everything changes for my family, and I would probably become the mandatory challenger," he said.

"I've got someone in front of me who is at the highest level. To even be in the ring with him means I've completed boxing in a way, regardless of what happens.

"I'm a lad from north Wales who only had an ambition of winning a Welsh title. To step in with a world champion is what dreams are made of."

articles.title: Viddal Riley: How Briton went from KSI's trainer to brink of world-title shot
articles.summary: Viddal Riley - who defends his European cruiserweight title on Saturday - talks through his journey from training YouTuber KSI to nearing a world-title shot.
articles.body:
Viddal Riley had spent years learning how to fight. Then he taught a YouTuber, and that became the story.

On Saturday, the Londoner defends his European cruiserweight title against unbeaten Frenchman Seydi Coupe at Wembley Arena, with a world-title shot within reach.

Yet it was his work with social media star KSI that first brought him mainstream attention, training the YouTuber for his fights against Joe Weller and Logan Paul.

From a corner of boxing where popularity can secure a headline fight before a punch has been thrown, Riley, 29, arrived with credentials few of his new audience knew about.

"I didn't do all that hard work from such a young age to just be known as a trainer of a famous person," he tells BBC Sport.

"I can't push away something that's part of my story. I just wanted to make sure that's not the only thing I'm known as and I've managed to do that."

Riley, unbeaten in 14 professional fights, first entered a boxing gym aged six and was national champion at 11.

He collected eight titles in the amateurs, representing Team GB and captaining England before meeting KSI at 19.

English, British and European titles have followed as a professional. He thought beating Cheavon Clarke might win over the sceptics, but the influencer tag has proved hard to shift.

"I'm pretty much giving up on trying to convince a purist of what I am," he says. "If you can't read facts and figures to convince yourself, then you're in your own world."

From a YouTuber trainer to Mayweather and Mexico

When Riley went to Las Vegas as KSI's trainer, he made sure his own boxing kit was in the luggage. The trip came about because Floyd Mayweather Sr wanted to build his social media presence.

"I took it as an opportunity to showcase my abilities even though I was there as his trainer," he says.

Riley - who had already made his professional debut in Tijuana, Mexico in 2018 - sparred with established professionals and impressed enough to earn a deal with Mayweather Promotions the following year.

There had been moments, though, when Riley wondered whether life as a cornerman might suit him better.

"Seeing how they were living and how I could not be the one in danger and still make a good life for myself, it does make you second guess," he says.

But Riley wanted to pursue his own career. His first professional appearance in Britain would not come until his fifth fight.

Joining MF Pro - 'there's no loophole, there's no life hack'

Working with KSI taught Riley how to handle the media glare. He built an audience of his own and now has about 1.2 million YouTube subscribers.

"It got me accustomed to being in the limelight," he says. "Ready for the attention to be on me on a big stage."

After starting with Mayweather Promotions, Riley developed his career with Boxxer - winning English and British titles.

His points victory over Clarke looks better still after Clarke stopped former world champion Chris Billam-Smith last weekend.

"Some things take time to mature," Riley says. "It allows people to understand the level that I am and my capabilities."

Yet joining MF Pro in December 2025 risked bringing the conversation back to influencer boxing. Before signing with the professional venture affiliated with KSI's Misfits, Riley wanted the distinction made clear.

"Are you going to make this clear that I'm not joining Misfits Boxing?" he recalls asking. "I haven't done all of this hard work to then sign a professional contract that's going to drag me back into what I've worked so hard to differentiate myself from."

Riley says he had offers from "basically all promoters", but felt MF Pro best appreciated both his boxing and his audience. Assurances he could continue pursuing a world title made signing "a no-brainer".

He believes other fighters can learn from his approach, but warns against expecting a shortcut: "You can't skip anything. There's no loophole, there's no life hack or anything like that."

Victory over Mateusz Masternak secured an IBF mandatory position, with New Zealand's David Nyika lined up to face Riley for the vacant title. Those plans are being held up by former champion Jai Opetaia's legal dispute with the governing body.

The IBF stripped Opetaia after he fought Brandon Glanton despite it withdrawing approval for the bout. The Australian is challenging that decision while also stepping up to heavyweight to face Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua undercard in December.

"It's messy up there right now, but I'm trying to get in the mess," Riley says.

Rather than wait, he has opted to defend his European belt against Coupe, also unbeaten in 14 fights. He will not predict when his world-title opportunity might arrive.

"I'm just hyper-focused on Saturday. I can't go past Saturday," he says. "In my mind, the world ends on Saturday."

One name persuades him to look beyond it. Oleksandr Usyk, whose team say he is considering returning to cruiserweight, would be Riley's dream opponent.

"Much respect to him - he's a legend," he says. "But to be able to step in the ring with him and battle, that will be sick."

articles.title: Chantelle Cameron vs Mikaela Mayer rematch confirmed on undercard for Jake Paul vs Cedric Doumbe on Christmas Eve
articles.summary: Chantelle Cameron to face Mikaela Mayer in highly-anticipated rematch on the Jake Paul vs Cedric Doumbe bill on Christmas Eve in Dubai; Cameron claimed a hard-fought points win over Mayer in Birmingham in August; Paul makes his return to boxing on the Most Valuable Promotions show
articles.body:
Unified super-welterweight world champion Cameron will share the ring again with Mayer in Dubai just four months after she defeated the American in a thrilling fight in Birmingham.

In a fight of the year contender, Cameron claimed a hard-fought unanimous decision victory following a fiery build-up, and she is relishing the opportunity to face Mayer in a rematch on a huge Most Valuable Promotions show as Paul returns to the ring for the first time since his fight with Anthony Joshua.

"We agreed to the rematch before the first fight, so we both kept our word," said Cameron.

"And now the rematch is on the biggest stage in boxing."

After the first fight, Mayer claimed she should have been awarded the win, accusing Cameron of being "lucky in her little back yard".

The 36-year-old American is now looking to reclaim her world champion status.

"Although I don't feel I performed to my highest potential, I've been working hard to fix the mistakes I made and I will 100 per cent come back stronger," she said.

"I'm taking my belts back on Thursday, December 24."

The Paul vs Doumbe bill also features undefeated US Olympian and 2021 amateur world champion Jahmal Harvey (5-0, 4 KOs) who faces Scotland's Craig Morgan (15-1-1) in an eight-round lightweight bout at 135 lbs.

Nakisa Bidarian, CEO of Most Valuable Promotions, said: "Chantelle Cameron vs Mikaela Mayer 2 marks MVP's latest seismic pound-for-pound clash with two of the world's top ten fighters meeting again in their prime.

"Their first meeting just a few months ago was a clear 'Fight of the Year' contender and both immediately called for the rematch following the fight - a testament to both being willing to take on the hardest challenges.

"Now the stakes rise even higher for Chantelle as she puts three titles on the line against a hungry Mayer, one of the sport's biggest faces in her own right and a US Olympian.

"They are joined by USA's knockout sensation and future face of the lightweight division Jahmal Harvey. Topped by an unmissable Jake Paul vs Cedric Doumbe main event, MVP's Christmas Eve spectacle only gets bigger and better."

Doumbe, a former two-time Glory welterweight kickboxing champion, boasts an impressive 75-7-1 record in kickboxing, including 45 knockouts.

He is also 6-1 in mixed martial arts and 1-0 as a professional boxer, having beaten Mohamed Fodil on points in his sole boxing appearance back in 2015.

articles.title: UFC 334: I don't like Josh Hokit antics but he deserves title shot, says Dana White
articles.summary: UFC president Dana White says he doesn't like Josh Hokit's "shtick" but he has earned his heavyweight title shot against Ciryl Gane at UFC 334.
articles.body:
UFC president Dana White says he doesn't like Josh Hokit's "shtick" but he has earned his heavyweight title shot against Ciryl Gane.

American Hokit will face Frenchman Gane for the undisputed heavyweight title at UFC 334 at New York's Madison Square Garden on Saturday.

Hokit is a controversial fighter, who in a similar vein to Colby Covington, adopts various personas during interviews to generate attention from fans.

He has been accused of overstepping the line into discrimination, however, after making racially aggravated and misogynistic comments in his post-UFC 324 interview in January.

After Hokit directed misogynistic comments towards former First Lady Michelle Obama in June, UFC president Dana White described his words as "gross", "moronic", and "inappropriate".

Hokit directed more crude jokes towards his fellow fighters during a news conference to promote UFC 334, but White defended the 29-year-old.

"You know how I feel about shtick, I don't like them, I don't like his shtick, but for anyone to say he doesn't deserve this fight is crazy," said White.

"He earned this fight, that he absolutely did."

Hokit will fight for the heavyweight title despite only making his UFC debut one year ago.

Since then he has won four fights in the promotion, to extend his unbeaten record to 10.

Some critics have argued he doesn't deserve a title shot yet in place of fighters such as Alexander Volkov, and he has been awarded it because his controversial comments generate attention.

Gane, who is defending the belt for the first time since being upgraded to undisputed heavyweight champion in September when Tom Aspinall vacated the title , disagrees.

"Honestly he deserves it, he's a great athlete, he's done very well, and he has a big mouth also that is good for the business," said Gane.

"This is his character. I understand it, and I'm comfortable with it."

Hokit poked fun at the 36-year-old Frenchman during the news conference by wearing goggles and an eye patch, in reference to Gane's fight with Aspinall in 2025.

The bout ended in a no-contest after eye-pokes from Gane left Aspinall unable to continue.

Aspinall later accused Gane of cheating, but the Frenchman says it was accidental.

Gane consistently saw the funny side to Hokit's antics, as he laughed off the majority of comments from the challenger.

"He's a smart guy, people underestimate him. He's a good fighter also, he's a good wrestler and I think he has a good fight IQ," Gane told BBC Sport.

"He creates the character and that's smart, this is a business also. But he's not here only because of that that, he's also 10-0 and on a good run."

"Men lie, women lie, numbers don't, I earned my spot and this position, and I'm grateful for it," said Hokit.

UFC 334: Gane v Hokit - all you need to know

The co-main event features Kayla Harrison defending the women's bantamweight title against returning hall-of-famer Amanda Nunes.

American Harrison is fighting for the first time since neck and spinal surgery in January, while Brazil's Nunes is coming out of retirement after leaving the sport and her glittering career behind in 2023.

Nunes is a former bantamweight and featherweight champion and is widely regarded as one of the best mixed martial artists of all time.

The pair used to be team-mates at American Top Team Gym before Nunes left in 2022, but got involved in a heated back and forth in the news conference.

"Look in my eyes. If you don't respect that I can beat you on Saturday, you're not supposed to be a champion," said Nunes.

Harrison responded by saying: "I respect everyone, but fear no-one," as the pair argued for almost two minutes.

White later had to guide Harrison away as the pair went face to face in an intense stare-down.

Earlier White criticised fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili for their part in a mass brawl in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday which led to 10 arrests.

A video of the incident appeared to show Russian Nurmagomedov slap Dvalishvili after approaching the Georgian from behind.

Fighting then broke out between the two and members of their teams in a hotel lobby, with Abu Dhabi police confirming the arrests.

White called the altercation "ridiculous" and "stupid", and referred to the participants as "a bunch of idiots".

articles.title: Fury v Joshua: Joe Cordina unlikely to face Manny Pacquiao in Cardiff
articles.summary: Joe Cordina's hopes of facing boxing great Manny Pacquiao on December's Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua card in Cardiff appear to be over.
articles.body:
Joe Cordina's hopes of facing all-time great Manny Pacquiao on the undercard of December's Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua showdown appear to be over.

The 34-year-old former IBF super-featherweight champion wanted to face Pacquiao, 47, on home soil at the Principality Stadium on 11 December.

The Cardiff undercard is not yet complete, but so far features only heavyweight clashes as support to the all-British affair between Fury and Joshua.

Deontay Wilder vs Jai Opetaia, Da'Mazion Vanhouter vs Michael Essomba and Martin Bakole vs Solomon Adebayo are the other bouts confirmed so far.

Cordina's promoter Eddie Hearn - who has been critical of the announced undercard - says he has "lined up a big fight for Cordina in January".

Facing Pacquiao in Cardiff would be honour for Cordina

Workaholic with a tattooed throat – meet The Merthyr Mexican

Reports indicate that Pacquiao, a 12-time world champion across eight different weights, may also have settled on facing an opponent in early 2027 instead, with an official announcement expected soon.

While Cordina had agreed terms to face Pacquiao, the Filipino legend - who has not fought since July 2025 - has not reciprocated.

Hearn previously admitted that he was unsure whether the final details could be agreed.

But the promoter has been adamant in his belief that a Welsh fighter must feature on what is one of the most highly anticipated boxing cards in recent years.

"Not having a two-time world champion from Wales on the undercard is crazy," Hearn told IFL TV.

Abdullah Mason, Shakur Stevenson and Keyshawn Davis are all fighters that Hearn has name-checked as potential opponents for Cordina if the Pacquiao showdown could not be finalised.

Turki Alalshikh, the co-founder of Zuffa Boxing and a member of the Saudi Royal Court, has confirmed that the 11 December card is not yet finalised.

images.caption: Image caption, Boxing great Manny Pacquiao (left) is leaning towards a fight in early 2027 rather than facing Joe Cordina

articles.title: Updated 2026 AEW Full Gear Card and Predictions for Match Order
articles.summary: Most of AEW's top championships will be up for grabs Saturday when Full Gear descends upon Phoenix, Arizona.
articles.body:
Most of AEW's top championships will be up for grabs Saturday when Full Gear descends upon Phoenix, Arizona.

Chief among them is the AEW World Championship held by Will Ospreay, as he is set to defend against longtime friend and now rival Kyle Fletcher in the likely main event.

Additionally, Mercedes Moné is putting the AEW women's world title on the line against Marina Shafir, and Anarchy in the Arena will make its return to AEW when The Death Riders and The Conglomeration clash with The Cut.

Here is a rundown of the Full Gear card, complete with predictions for the match order and a closer look at the top bouts to watch.

Where: Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona

When: Saturday, Nov. 14 at 8 p.m. ET (Zero Hour pre-show starts at 7 p.m. ET)

Watch: HBO Max, Prime Video, DAZN, Fubo, PPV.com

AEW Full Gear Card and Projected Match Order

Pre-Show TBS Championship Three-Way Match: Queen Aminata (c) vs. Persephone vs. Maya World

AEW World Tag Team Championship: The Young Bucks (c) vs. Mark Davis & Jake Doyle

National Championship: Tommaso Ciampa (c) vs. Ilja Dragunov

AEW Women's World Tag Team Championship: Brawling Birds (Jamie Hayter & Alex Windsor) (c) vs. Wrathlander (Kris Statlander & Harley Cameron)

International Championship: Kazuchika Okada (c) vs. Adam Copeland

AEW World Trios Championship Texas Deathmatch: "Hangman" Adam Page & Brodido (Brody King & Bandido) (c) vs. Swerve Strickland & The New Level (Kofi & Austin Creed)

AEW Women's World Championship: Mercedes Moné (c) vs. Marina Shafir

Anarchy in the Arena: The Death Riders (Jon Moxley, Daniel Garcia & Gabe Kidd) & The Conglomeration (Orange Cassidy, Kyle O'Reilly & Roderick Strong) vs. The Cut (Jay White, David Finlay, Clark Connors, Austin Gunn, Colten Gunn & Ace Austin)

AEW World Championship: Will Ospreay (c) vs. Kyle Fletcher

Regarded by many as two of the top in-ring performers in wrestling today, Will Ospreay and Kyle Fletcher will meet at Full Gear with the AEW World Championship hanging in the balance.

Ospreay and Fletcher have wrestled each other many times before, but the stakes were never this high on the previous occasions.

That suggests both stars will put their best foot forward and be fully committed to delivering a match that fans will remember for a long time to come.

Ospreay has not been shy about meeting challenges head on since winning the AEW world title at All In, while Fletcher has been a star on the rise for quite some time.

The next major step for Fletcher to take is to become a world champion, and while it is fair to wonder if that will be in the cards for him at Full Gear, all signs point toward him winning the big one eventually.

Adam Copeland announced that 2027 will be his final year as an active wrestler, and he is getting a head start on some of the numerous dream matches fans would love to see him have before he steps away for good.

One of them will come to fruition at Full Gear when Cope challenges Kazuchika Okada for the International Championship.

Over the past few weeks, Copeland and Okada have mixed it up on a couple of occasions, but never in a singles match.

Okada got a pinfall on Copeland during the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream, and Okada's team later beat Copeland's team in Blood & Guts.

As a result, Copeland will be out for revenge, and if he comes out on top, he will win his third different championship since joining AEW.

For the first time since making his AEW debut last month at WrestleDream, Ilja Dragunov will compete in an AEW pay-per-view match at Full Gear.

The contest will have significant stakes attached to it as well with Dragunov challenging Tommaso Ciampa for the National Championship he just won from Andrade El Idolo.

Ciampa and Dragunov are two of the hardest-hitting and most-believable wrestlers in the game today, so they figure to deliver a high level of physicality on Saturday.

Helping the cause is the fact that Ciampa and Dragunov are already familiar with each other, having faced off in WWE previously.

With some chemistry already present for them to build upon, the groundwork is laid for Ciampa and Dragunov to have a bout that challenges for match of the night honors.

articles.title: Dana White brands Usman Nurmagomedov-Merab Dvalishvili brawl ‘f***ing idiotic’ as 10 arrested and jailed in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: UFC President Dana White condemns Usman Nurmagomedov's altercation with Merab Dvalishvili in Abu Dhabi, leading to multiple arrests and raising questions about Nurmagomedov's future in the UFC.
articles.body: UFC president Dana White has delivered a blunt assessment of the altercation between Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili in Abu Dhabi, describing those involved as “f***ing idiots” after police made multiple arrests. The incident has also raised questions about Nurmagomedov's potential future in the UFC, particularly after the promotion had been linked with the highly regarded lightweight in recent weeks.Dana White condemns Abu Dhabi brawl and arrestsWhite addressed the confrontation at the UFC 334 pre-fight press conference on Thursday, November 12, after being asked about the fight that left Dvalishvili bloodied and several people in police custody.“What a bunch of fing idiots,” White said. “It’s absolutely ridiculous and stupid and they’re all in jail. That is not a place to go f around.”The UFC president later offered a further assessment when approached by New York street journalist Adam Glyn, reiterating his concern about the impact of the incident on everyone involved.“That stuff is never good for business. It makes everyone involved look bad. It’s unfortunate. Now they’re all in jail in Abu Dhabi. We’ll see how that goes,” White said.The confrontation took place on Wednesday, November 11, at a hotel in Abu Dhabi, where Nurmagomedov interrupted Dvalishvili during an interview ahead of the Real American Freestyle (RAF) wrestling event. Footage circulating online showed Nurmagomedov approaching the Georgian fighter and slapping him before the situation escalated into a wider fight involving members of both groups.Dvalishvili subsequently shared footage showing his bloodied face, alleging that he and a friend had been attacked by Nurmagomedov and several members of his entourage. The incident prompted Abu Dhabi Police to confirm 10 arrests, with eight people detained over their alleged involvement in the fight and two others arrested for filming it. All those detained were referred to the Public Prosecution, although authorities have not identified the individuals arrested or confirmed whether Nurmagomedov or Dvalishvili was among them.Usman Nurmagomedov banned from RAF event as fight cards face uncertaintyThe incident occurred just days before RAF's first event in the Middle East, scheduled for Saturday, November 14, in Abu Dhabi. Dvalishvili was due to face Marlon Moraes, while Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's brother, was scheduled to compete against Urijah Faber.RAF co-founder Chad Bronstein confirmed that Usman had been banned from attending the event following the hotel confrontation. However, there has been no equivalent confirmation concerning Umar or Dvalishvili, leaving uncertainty over whether the two scheduled bouts will proceed as planned.Umar was also reportedly involved in the wider altercation, although the precise circumstances and individual roles remain subject to the police investigation. The arrests have added another complication to an event already facing scrutiny because of the confrontation between the two camps.The rivalry between the fighters also has an established sporting history. In early 2025, Dvalishvili retained his UFC bantamweight championship by defeating Umar on points. Umar subsequently suffered another setback in August when Song Yadong knocked him out.Usman entered the cage after that defeat and appeared to elbow Song as the Chinese fighter celebrated by running around the octagon. The incident attracted criticism, although many viewers considered the contact accidental. His latest confrontation with Dvalishvili has now brought renewed attention to his conduct outside competition.Will the incident affect Usman Nurmagomedov's potential UFC move?The timing of the confrontation is particularly significant because Nurmagomedov has been linked with a move to the UFC. The Russian, a cousin of former UFC lightweight champion Khabib Nurmagomedov, is widely regarded as one of the leading fighters in his division outside the promotion and had attracted considerable interest as a potential signing.However, White played down the immediate possibility of negotiations when asked about Nurmagomedov's situation at Thursday's press conference.“He’s still under contract [with the PFL]. We’re not talking him right now anyway,” White said.His comments also addressed speculation that Nurmagomedov was already a free agent after completing his most recent PFL contract. White's clarification indicates that, from the UFC's perspective, the Russian remains under contract with the organisation.The Abu Dhabi incident could nevertheless complicate his prospects if he eventually becomes available. The footage showing the initial slap and the subsequent group confrontation has attracted widespread criticism, while the police investigation and potential legal consequences introduce considerations beyond his record inside the cage.There has been speculation that the incident could weaken Nurmagomedov's negotiating position or affect the financial terms of a potential UFC agreement. However, White has not announced any disciplinary decision or ruled out signing him in the future. For now, his position is that the fighter remains under contract with the PFL, and the UFC is not discussing a deal with him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Booking Swerve Strickland's Path Back to AEW's World Championship
articles.summary: Swerve Strickland is gaining momentum as All Elite Wrestling's top antagonist, making this the ideal time for him to return to the world title picture.
articles.body:
Swerve Strickland is gaining momentum as All Elite Wrestling's top antagonist, making this the ideal time for him to return to the world title picture.

Two years ago, The Most Dangerous Man in AEW defeated Samoa Joe at Dynasty to become the company's first Black world champion. Strickland had a strong run before he ultimately dropped the title to Bryan Danielson at All In: London.

It was a career-defining reign that proved to mainstream fans that he had arrived as a legitimate main eventer. Anyone familiar with his work on the indies knew he had the potential, but his 2024 run confirmed how much he had grown as a performer.

So much so that many fans felt his reign ended too soon, especially after his last one-on-one match with "Hangman" Adam Page at All Out. Considering the reaction every time the two have crossed paths this year, it may be time to thrust their heated rivalry back into the main event scene.

Surprisingly, Strickland hasn't held the AEW World Championship again, but he's undeniably hot right now. The 36-year-old is in the best storyline with The New Level.

He consistently makes everyone he works with better, and his matches always deliver. This is how we would book his path back to the company's top prize.

His upcoming Texas Deathmatch for the trios titles could go either way. Hangman and Brodido could retain, giving The New Level the chance to venture into the tag division.

However, a win at Full Gear doesn't mean Strickland must abandon his pursuit of singles gold. In fact, his interactions with Page should remind both men why they sought to challenge each other at the event in 2023.

They both also have a history with the current champion, Will Ospreay, which provides another reason to chase the title. Their dynamic during the "Dynasty era" is the perfect foundation for an eventual triple threat match.

We never truly got a rewarding conclusion to their uneasy alliance at All In: Texas. Yes, Strickland and Ospreay faced off in this year's men's Owen Hart Cup finals, but there's so much more AEW could do with them.

The company should spend the remainder of 2026 positioning them to collide next year. Strickland overcomes Hangman at Full Gear, forcing him to admit the trios titles will never fill the void created after his loss to MJF.

Meanwhile, his bitter rival refocuses on his goal to regain the world title by any means necessary. An inevitable matchup with The Elite will keep him and The New Level occupied, but the ultimate move should be to call out Ospreay.

It's a safe bet that MJF will return before the end of the year and stake his claim to a title shot. After all, he still believes Kenny Omega only beat him because Ospreay intervened and that he is the real world champion.

This sets up their rematch at Worlds End, where The Aerial Assassin retains his title. Afterward, Strickland stands at the top of the ramp and watches him celebrate. Conversely, Hangman enters the Continental Classic and loses in the finals.

At New Year's Smash, Strickland reminds everyone of everything he accomplished with AEW and vows that 2027 will be his year. During the same episode, Andrade El Idolo uses his guaranteed title opportunity to call his shot at Dynasty.

Ospreay narrowly defeats him, but Strickland enters the ring afterward. He says, "I made history at this event three years ago. What do you say we make history again?"

Before they can shake hands, The Cut attacks them both, and Jay White picks up the AEW World Championship. Ospreay offers White a title match on the following episode of Dynamite, infuriating Strickland.

During their match, The Cut interferes to help White until The United Empire runs them off. The Switchblade lands The Blade Runner, but he gets hit with a House Call before he can pin Ospreay.

Ospreay wins with Strickland's help, but his longtime friend attacks him afterward until The New Level comes to his aid. To everyone's surprise, he shoves the Austin Creed and Kofi down and says, "I tried to do this the right way."

Over the next few weeks, Strickland continues to attack the champion and his stablemates. His promos get increasingly personal until Ospreay accepts his challenge. Hangman eventually steps in and points out that he's going too far again.

Page has seen what the most dangerous man is willing to do to win the world title, so he warns Ospreay he's making a mistake. Nevertheless, the match goes on as scheduled, and Strickland cheats to win.

The New Level reluctantly comes down to the ring, and he demands that they lift him up on their shoulders like Big E and Creed famously did. The closing shot is an homage to Kofi's win at WrestleMania 35, with Strickland sporting an evil grin.

Ospreay eventually demands a rematch, but Hangman interjects to go back on his word and challenge for the world title. He reasons that he believes he's the only one who can stop him, but neither will back down, setting up a triple threat for AEW Revolution.

Reports suggest that the event will take place in the spring next year. This match would be a fitting main event for the show.

articles.title: ‘We should do better as Muslims, human beings and athletes’: Usman Nurmagomedov’s manager apologises to Abu Dhabi leadership and people on behalf of his team after brawl
articles.summary: Usman Nurmagomedov’s manager Ali Abdelaziz has issued an apology to Abu Dhabi and its leadership following the violent confrontation involving members of
articles.body: Usman Nurmagomedov’s manager Ali Abdelaziz has issued an apology to Abu Dhabi and its leadership following the violent confrontation involving members of the Russian fighter’s camp and Merab Dvalishvili. With arrests made and the incident drawing criticism from the UFC, Abdelaziz has acknowledged that his team’s conduct was unacceptable, while admitting that the consequences extend well beyond the fighters directly involved.Ali Abdelaziz apologises to Abu Dhabi on behalf of Nurmagomedov and his teamSpeaking to MMA Junkie on Thursday, November 12, Abdelaziz expressed embarrassment over the incident and apologised to the people and leadership of Abu Dhabi, where the confrontation took place.“I'm truly sorry [about Wednesday's events]. It's embarrassing what happened. I hope these young men will get a good lesson. This is something that should not happen again.“All of our guys have to set a good example [...] I haven't slept for a couple days, trying to make it better. I don't think there's any words I can say to make this better. To the people of Abu Dhabi, to the leadership, this is something that will never happen again.“We should do better as Muslims, as human beings, as athletes [...] What happened was something unacceptable and should never happen again.”Abdelaziz also made clear that the apology was not limited to Nurmagomedov's individual conduct, but extended to the wider group associated with him. He acknowledged that the incident had been deeply disrespectful to the host city and that the fighters involved had a responsibility to represent themselves and their teams appropriately.The confrontation occurred on Wednesday, November 11, at a hotel in Abu Dhabi, where Dvalishvili was recording an interview ahead of the Real American Freestyle wrestling event. Footage showed Nurmagomedov approaching the Georgian fighter from behind and slapping him, triggering a wider fight involving members of both groups. Dvalishvili and a friend attempted to defend themselves against Nurmagomedov and several members of his entourage, with the former UFC bantamweight champion subsequently sharing footage of his bloodied face.Abu Dhabi Police confirmed 10 arrests following the incident, with eight people detained over their alleged involvement in the fight and two others for filming it. Those arrested were referred to the Public Prosecution. Authorities have not publicly identified the individuals detained.Abdelaziz says neither side was justified in the confrontationThe manager also addressed suggestions that Dvalishvili's previous comments about Team Nurmagomedov had contributed to the confrontation or justified the response. Abdelaziz rejected that argument, insisting that previous disagreements could not excuse what happened at the hotel.“Two wrongs doesn't make a right. I'm not going to sit here and say he did that or he didn't do that. These guys are young, and there's no words I can describe to say he was wrong. I think both parties were wrong, and two wrongs don't make a right, and it's a good lesson for everyone. Merab was there a couple weeks ago. He was fine and trained at Khabib's gym. I think we have to do better as humans. We have to learn from this mistake. I'm not going to point fingers. It was extremely disrespectful to the people of Abu Dhabi, to the city of Abu Dhabi. We have to be better and conduct ourselves better. This situation could've been handled different but I understand these athletes are emotional. But there's no excuse. There's no excuse. There's nothing I can say to make the wrong situation better.”His reference to Dvalishvili training at Khabib Nurmagomedov's gym came amid the wider relationship between the Georgian fighter and the Dagestani camp. Abdelaziz did not attempt to assign responsibility for the confrontation through their previous disagreements, instead acknowledging that the situation could have been handled differently and that emotional reactions were no justification for violence.The apology follows criticism from UFC president Dana White, who described those involved as “a bunch of fing idiots” and called the incident “absolutely ridiculous and stupid” during a press conference on Thursday. White also said the confrontation was “not a place to go f around”, referring to the fact that those arrested were being held in Abu Dhabi.Usman Nurmagomedov’s career and the wider team face consequencesAbdelaziz acknowledged that the incident could affect more than Usman Nurmagomedov's immediate future, with the repercussions potentially extending to his cousin Khabib Nurmagomedov and the wider team.“About Usman's career: The guy is one of the best fighters in the world. Of course this is going to affect everybody. It's going to affect him, Khabib, everybody. But I'm not worried about his fighting career right now. I'm worried about his well-being and how he's going to recover from this,” he told MMA Junkie.The manager's comments come at a difficult moment for Nurmagomedov, who had attracted attention as a potential UFC signing after completing his latest contract with the Professional Fighters League. However, White clarified on Thursday that the Russian remained under contract with the PFL and that the UFC was not currently discussing a deal with him.“He’s still under contract [with the PFL]. We’re not talking him right now anyway,” White said.Nurmagomedov has also been banned from attending Saturday's RAF event in Abu Dhabi, a decision confirmed by co-founder Chad Bronstein. Dvalishvili was scheduled to face Marlon Moraes at the November 14 event, while Usman's brother Umar was due to compete against Urijah Faber. Their participation remains uncertain following the confrontation, with no equivalent announcement confirming that either Umar or Dvalishvili has been barred.Abdelaziz's apology has addressed the wider team's responsibility and the offence caused to Abu Dhabi, but the legal proceedings remain separate. With those detained referred to the Public Prosecution, the authorities will determine the next steps in the case.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: El gran día de Josh Hokit, el peleador más polémico de la UFC que puede ser campeón de peso pesado
articles.standfirst: El estadounidense se enfrentará a Ciryl Gane este sábado en el combate estelar del UFC 334 con el cinturón en juego
articles.summary: El estadounidense se enfrentará a Ciryl Gane este sábado en el combate estelar del UFC 334 con el cinturón en juego
articles.body: En apenas un año, Josh Hokit (10-0) ha pasado de debutar en la UFC a encabezar la cartelera del UFC 334 en el Madison Square Garden -Nueva York- para medirse a Ciryl Gane (14-2) e intentar arrebatarle el cinturón de peso pesado. El peleador estadounidense se ha convertido en el tipo más polémico de la compañía con sus constantes salidas de tono, pero eso le ha ayudado a que en apenas cinco peleas con la promotora ya haya gozado de una oportunidad titular. Antes de entrar en sus polémicas hay que conocer al peleador, ya que Hokit viene de una carrera fallida en la NFL que le convirtió en un atleta de élite mucho antes de dar el salto a la UFC. En agosto de 2025, Josh se ganó un contrato con la compañía tras finalizar a su oponente en las Dana White's Contender Series, y tras debutar con K.O. el 8 de noviembre de 2025 ha sumado otras tres victorias más que le han catapultado al estrellato. Su primer gran triunfo fue ante Curtis Blaydes en abril, ya que a pesar de ser un grappler demostró ser uno de los pesos pesados más entretenidos en el striking. Ambos protagonizaron uno de los mejores combates del año, y Hokit no paró de provocar a su rival durante el combate sacándole el dedo y mostrando un pundonor inaudito. Esto, además, provocó que esa misma noche Dana White -jefe de la UFC- y Donald Trump hablasen para incluirle en el UFC Casa Blanca del 14 de junio, donde noqueó a Derrick Lewis. Tras la lesión ocular de Tom Aspinall que le ha obligado a dejar vacante su cinturón, Ciryl Gane se convirtió en campeón indiscutido y la UFC ha decidido enfrentarle contra Hokit en uno de los escenarios más emblemáticos del mundo. Al Madison Square Garden solo acuden estrellas, y ambos encabezarán uno de los eventos del año. Ahora bien, hay una frase que se repite en el mundo de las MMA: 'Respeto a Josh Hokit por lo que es como peleador, a pesar de sus constantes salidas de tono'. Hasta el propio Dana White ha afirmado que no está de acuerdo con todo lo que suelta el estadounidense por la boca, ya que para él no hay límites a la hora de insultar a sus rivales. Se ha vomitado encima durante un pesaje, ha sacado un tema de rap insultando a toda la división de peso pesado, e incluso se ha llegado a encarar con Ilia Topuria durante una rueda de prensa. De hecho, tras su victoria en el UFC Casa Blanca cogió el micro y dijo una frase que tuvo que ser censurada de la retransmisión a posteriori. "Michelle Obama es un hombre". Fue preguntado hace poco al respecto, y afirma que no se arrepiente. Sin ir más lejos, Ciryl Gane dijo que lo único que no quería es que Hokit se metiese con su madre, y eso fue lo primero que hizo el estadounidense nada más sentarse en la rueda de prensa de la pasada madrugada. Al escucharle muchos tienen una concepción errónea de Josh, ya que en realidad es una persona muy inteligente. En sus campamentos sigue durmiendo en el gimnasio en el que empezó para no olvidar sus orígenes, y cuando se sale del personaje demuestra ser un tipo muy sensato. Sin embargo, una vez entra en su papel no hay nada ni nadie que se le ponga por delante, y eso le ha permitido crecer tan rápido en la compañía. De hecho, anoche volvió a ser el protagonista principal de la rueda de prensa, y su discurso tiene cada vez más adeptos. Este sábado 21 de noviembre tendrá la oportunidad de convertirse en campeón de peso pesado con 29 años y toda una carrera por delante. Además, él ha afirmado que podría cortar de peso perfectamente y bajar incluso a peso medio, pero su objetivo es demostrar que es un atleta de élite y que puede arrasar a cualquiera sin necesidad de ser un 'weight bully'. Mañana será su momento de demostrarlo ante uno de los mejores pesos pesados de los últimos años.

articles.title: Usman Nurmagomedov and team reportedly sentenced to six months in prison, AED 300,000 fines and deportation for attacking UFC fighter Dvalishvili
articles.summary: Usman Nurmagomedov's entourage faces six months in prison, hefty fines, and deportation following a violent altercation with UFC fighter Merab Dvalishvili in Abu Dhabi. Find out how this incident could impact Nurmagomedov's future in the UFC.
articles.body: The Abu Dhabi Criminal Court has handed down prison sentences, substantial fines and deportation orders following the hotel brawl involving Usman Nurmagomedov’s entourage and former UFC champion Merab Dvalishvili. Ten people have been convicted over the confrontation, with the authorities imposing separate penalties on those involved in the fight and two individuals who recorded and published footage of it. Dvalishvili and a friend were also fined, although neither received a prison sentence.Abu Dhabi court sentences eight people to six months in prisonThe Abu Dhabi Judicial Department confirmed that six defendants involved in the confrontation were sentenced to six months in prison, fined AED 300,000 each (approximately $81,700) and ordered to be deported from the United Arab Emirates after completing their sentences.The convictions concerned disturbing public security, causing panic and endangering lives, following the violent altercation at a hotel on Yas Island. The authorities have not publicly identified the six defendants, so it remains unclear whether Usman Nurmagomedov himself was among those sentenced.The court also handed six-month prison sentences to the two individuals who filmed the confrontation and subsequently published footage of it. They received the same AED 300,000 fine (approximately $81,700) each and were ordered to be deported after serving their sentences.Their convictions concerned violations of privacy through the use of information technology to record and publish footage of the brawl. The court additionally ordered their mobile phones to be confiscated and the recordings to be deleted.The ruling means eight of the 10 convicted individuals received prison sentences, financial penalties and deportation orders, although the specific identities of those sentenced have not been disclosed.Merab Dvalishvili and friend fined as RAF confirms his releaseDvalishvili and a friend were also penalised by the court, receiving fines of AED 50,000 each (approximately $13,600) for disturbing public security and assaulting others. Neither was sentenced to imprisonment.Real American Freestyle (RAF) CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein subsequently confirmed that Dvalishvili had been released and was back with the organisation's team in Abu Dhabi. In a statement issued later on Friday, November 13, Bronstein thanked the local authorities for their assistance.“I am pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi. We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support. We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us,” Bronstein said.The incident occurred on Wednesday, November 11, at the hotel hosting the RAF event, where Dvalishvili was conducting an interview ahead of his scheduled wrestling appearance. Nurmagomedov approached the Georgian fighter and slapped him, triggering a wider confrontation involving members of both groups. Dvalishvili and a friend were subsequently seen attempting to defend themselves against several members of Nurmagomedov's entourage.The confrontation reportedly stemmed from an earlier incident in August at RAF Georgia, where Dvalishvili allegedly slapped Ahmed Gadzhimagomedov, a friend of Usman's brother Umar Nurmagomedov, backstage. The reported earlier altercation has been cited as the motive for the confrontation in Abu Dhabi, although it does not change the penalties imposed by the court.What the sentences mean for Usman Nurmagomedov and his UFC futureThe court's decision comes at a significant point in Nurmagomedov's career. The undefeated Russian, who holds the PFL lightweight championship, had recently completed his contract with the promotion and declined to sign a new agreement. He had consequently been widely expected to become a target for the UFC, with his manager Ali Abdelaziz representing several fighters in the organisation.The confrontation has already drawn criticism from UFC president Dana White, who described those involved as “a bunch of f***ing idiots” and called the incident “absolutely ridiculous and stupid”. Abdelaziz also apologised to Abu Dhabi and its leadership on behalf of Nurmagomedov and his team, describing what happened as embarrassing and unacceptable.White had previously clarified that Nurmagomedov remained under contract with the PFL and that the UFC was not discussing a potential signing with him at that stage. The court's ruling adds another complication to questions surrounding his next career move, although the authorities have not clearly identified him as one of the individuals sentenced.Nurmagomedov had travelled to Abu Dhabi to support his brother Umar, who was scheduled to face former UFC champion Urijah Faber at Saturday's RAF event. Usman was subsequently banned from attending the competition following the hotel confrontation, while Dvalishvili had been scheduled to wrestle Marlon Moraes. Bronstein's confirmation of Dvalishvili's release means the Georgian is back with the RAF team, although the wider consequences of the incident for the fighters and their respective camps remain to be seen.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chantelle Cameron-Mikaela Mayer rematch added to Jake Paul v Cedric Doumbe 24 December card
articles.summary: Chantelle Cameron will defend her light-middleweight world titles in a rematch against Mikaela Mayer on the undercard of Jake Paul's fight against Cedric Doumbe on 24 December.
articles.body:
Chantelle Cameron will defend her light-middleweight world titles in a rematch against Mikaela Mayer on the undercard of Jake Paul's fight against Cedric Doumbe on 24 December.

Britain's Cameron beat Mayer by unanimous decision in August in an engrossing encounter to add the WBA and WBC titles to her WBO belt.

American Mayer, 36, disagreed with the decision, before an angry exchange of words between the pair, which opened up the possibility of a rematch.

Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) has confirmed the second bout between the two rivals will serve as the co-main at the Coca Cola Arena on Christmas Eve in Dubai.

MVP co-founder Paul takes on MMA fighter Doumbe in the main event in the American's first fight since being knocked out by Anthony Joshua last December.

Cameron, 35, will be aiming for her 24th win in 25 professional fights, with her only defeat coming against Katie Taylor in 2023.

"We agreed to the rematch before the first fight, so we both kept our word," said Cameron.

"And now the rematch is on the biggest stage in boxing."

Mayer has won 22 of her 25 professional fights, and is looking to reclaim her world titles.

"Although I don't feel I performed to my highest potential, I've been working hard to fix the mistakes I made and I will 100% come back stronger," she said.

"I'm taking my belts back on Thursday 24 December."

articles.body: La justicia en Abu Dhabi, Emiratos Árabes Unidos, no se ha hecho esperar. La corte de la ciudad emiratí ha anunciado las condenas por la multitudinaria pelea que tuvo lugar en un hotel de Yas Island el pasado miércoles, en la previa del evento de RAF Wrestling, y que implicaba a Usman Nurmagomedov, primo de Khabib y campeón de PFL, y Merab Dvalishvili, ex campeón de UFC y amigo de Ilia Topuria. Merab fue 'asaltado' por la espalda mientras grababa un vídeo y agredido por Usman Nurmagomedov con una bofetada. El daguestaní, acompañado de varios compañeros, atacó al georgiano, que iba únicamente con un amigo, el ahora viral Saba Lazishvili, produciéndose una pelea masiva en el 'hall' del hotel. Después de que 10 personas acabaran casi 48 horas bajo custodia policial, la corte de Abu Dhabi ha emitido un veredicto: Queda por ver si las entradas en prisión son firmes o no... pero la corte, en su comunicado, anuncia que las deportaciones se producirán después de que los acusados cumplan la pena. Por lo tanto, se entiende que sí. Merab y Saba, mientras, ya están en libertad y competirán en RAF Wrestling este sábado. Merab se iba a enfrentar a Moraes, y se mantiene su pelea de lucha... mientras que Saba ha sido 'fichado' y se medirá a toda una leyenda como Urijah Faber. articles.title: Dana White criticizes Team Khabib after Usman Nurmagomedov hotel attack leaves 8 jailed in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: UFC CEO Dana White denounced the attack on Merab Dvalishvili and took aim at the team of UFC Hall of Famer Khabib Nurmagomedov following Wednesday's brutal a...
articles.body:
UFC CEO Dana White denounced the attack on Merab Dvalishvili and took aim at the team of UFC Hall of Famer Khabib Nurmagomedov following Wednesday's brutal attack in Abu Dhabi that left eight individuals jailed in the Middle Eastern country for the next six months .

Tensions between Team Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili hit a boiling point Wednesday when shocking footage emerged of Usman Nurmagomedov jumping Dvalishvili and another individual, Saba Lazishvili, in a vicious group attack in a hotel lobby in Abu Dhabi prior to Saturday's RAF event. The attack left Dvalishvili badly bloodied and resulted in prison sentences, fines and eventual deportations for Nurmagomedov and seven others.

Umar Nurmagomedov, the younger brother of Usman, has publicly feuded with Dvalishvili since the two collided in a heated grudge match at UFC 311 in January 2025, which Dvalishvili won via unanimous decision to defend his UFC bantamweight title.

Speaking to former UFC heavyweight Stefan Struve on UFC op Eurosport , White pointed out that outside-of-the-cage brawls seem to follow the Nurmagomedovs — a team which is lead, in part, by retired former UFC lightweight champion Khabib Nurmagomedov:

"Anywhere the whole Khabib [Nurmagomedov] crew shows up, there's usually some fights going on, or Khamzat [Chimaev] and all these guys. And the RAF, I mean, there's literally a fist-fight at every single one of these things. "The RAF guys, you'd think they would learn after a couple of these and figure out how to stop this from happening. And people always ask me, 'Oh, isn't this good for you?' No, it's never good. "[I] don't like it, and obviously it's super dangerous. And to do it in a place like the Middle East? And what if any of you get seriously injured?"

"Anywhere the whole Khabib [Nurmagomedov] crew shows up, there's usually some fights going on, or Khamzat [Chimaev] and all these guys. And the RAF, I mean, there's literally a fist-fight at every single one of these things.

"The RAF guys, you'd think they would learn after a couple of these and figure out how to stop this from happening. And people always ask me, 'Oh, isn't this good for you?' No, it's never good.

"[I] don't like it, and obviously it's super dangerous. And to do it in a place like the Middle East? And what if any of you get seriously injured?"

White previously called Usman Nurmagomedov and everyone involved in the attack on Dvalishvili "a bunch of f***ing idiots" at UFC 334's pre-fight press conference on Thursday.

"It's absolutely ridiculous and stupid and they're all in jail," White said. "That is not a place to go f*** around."

Usman Nurmagomedov's actions have drawn swift condemnation from around the MMA world, however UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev — the No. 1-ranked pound-for-pound fighter in the sport and a fellow member of Team Khabib — defended the attack in a Wednesday post on social media , stating that "whatever happened today, was started by Merab," and questioning why critics were "silent when Merab slapped the Dagestani fighter and insulted his honor?"

Dvalishvili infamously slapped a friend and training partner of the Nurmagomedov clan, Ahmed Gadzhimagomedov, in a backstage altercation prior to the RAF Georgia event in Tbilisi, Georgia this past July . Gadzhimagomedov allegedly approached Dvalishvili after the event's pre-match press conference, grabbed him and aggressively asked in Russian what the former UFC bantamweight champion's problem was with Umar Nurmagomedov.

Usman Nurmagomedov is the reigning PFL lightweight champion and, until Wednesday's attack, was considered to be one of the top free agents available on MMA's open market. The UFC had been heavily linked to potentially signing him prior to the attack, however any talks will now have to be shelved until the end of his Abu Dhabi prison sentence.

In total, Usman Nurmagomedov was one of eight defendants to receive a six-month sentence, a fine of 300,000 UAE Dirhams (approximately $81,688) and deportation from the country following their stays behind bars.

Dvalishvili and Lazishvili have been fined 50,000 UAE Dirhams (approximately $13,600) each but did not receive jail time.

articles.title: Josh Hokit says he will ‘never’ regret vulgar Michelle Obama remarks, insists he is ‘proud’ of controversy ahead of UFC title fight
articles.summary: UFC heavyweight Josh Hokit defends his controversial remarks about Michelle Obama, claiming he is proud of the attention it has brought him as he prepares for a championship fight against Ciryl Gane at UFC 334.
articles.body: Josh Hokit has no intention of apologising for the remarks about former first lady Michelle Obama that drew widespread condemnation after his victory at the White House earlier this year. The undefeated heavyweight has instead defended his decision to make the comments, insisting that the setting was appropriate and that the controversy helped establish his public profile ahead of his first UFC championship opportunity.Josh Hokit doubles down on Michelle Obama remarks ahead of UFC 334Hokit reiterated his position during a media appearance at a New York hotel on Wednesday, November 11, two days before he challenges Ciryl Gane for the UFC heavyweight championship in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden.Asked whether he regretted his comments about Obama, the 28-year-old was unequivocal.“I'll never look back and be like, I regret that,” Hokit said.The heavyweight, who wore a black stocking cap over an American flag bandana, sunglasses and fight gloves, acknowledged that insulting the former first lady was not the right thing to do. However, he said he was proud that the controversy had brought him attention, including appearances in posts shared by US President Donald Trump on Truth Social.Hokit described himself as having “took the rap of a villain” before launching into what he called a freestyle rap to reinforce his position. He also defended making the remarks at the White House, arguing that the location represented freedom of speech.“I'm here to take what's mine,” Hokit said. “If I've got to rub some people the wrong way, if I've got to say some (stuff) in the wrong location, it is what it is. Was it not a good location to say it? I mean, we're at the White House. That house represents freedom of speech. So it is what it is. I think it was the perfect location to say it.”His comments came after he again directed a series of crude insults at other fighters on the UFC 334 card during Wednesday's appearance.What Josh Hokit said about Michelle Obama at the White HouseThe controversy began on June 14, 2026, when Hokit used his Octagon interview with Joe Rogan to repeat an unfounded conspiracy theory targeting Michelle Obama.Following his TKO victory over Derrick Lewis at UFC Freedom 250, an event held on the White House South Lawn to mark Trump's 80th birthday, Hokit declared: “Michelle Obama is a man, am I right, America?”The remark prompted criticism from across the political and sporting worlds. Republican Senator Lindsey Graham called Hokit an “idiot”, arguing that the comments detracted from the celebratory atmosphere of the event. Democratic lawmakers and former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III were also among those who condemned the attack.Trump subsequently shared posts featuring Hokit on Truth Social. One depicted the heavyweight in cartoon form alongside UFC chief Dana White inside the White House briefing room, giving the fighter further visibility as the controversy continued.White, however, made clear that he did not endorse Hokit's remarks. The UFC chief described them as “nasty”, “false” and “gross”, stressing that the fighter's views did not represent the organisation. White also acknowledged that he had given Hokit difficult opponents during his progression through the heavyweight rankings because he disliked “anything Josh Hokit says”.Josh Hokit puts undefeated record on the line against Ciryl GaneHokit's remarks have returned to the spotlight as he prepares for the biggest fight of his career. The 28-year-old enters UFC 334 with an unbeaten professional record of 10-0 and has won all six of his fights since joining the promotion in 2025.His victory over Lewis at the White House was the most prominent moment of his UFC career until now, but Saturday's contest carries considerably greater sporting significance. A win over Gane would make Hokit the UFC heavyweight champion, placing him at the top of a division in which the Frenchman is the reigning titleholder.Gane represents a substantial test for an undefeated contender who has built much of his public profile through outspoken behaviour outside the cage. Hokit has shown little interest in retreating from that approach, even as his comments about Obama continue to attract criticism.For now, he appears content to accept the consequences of the attention he has generated. His immediate task, however, is to turn an unbeaten record and a growing public profile into a championship victory at Madison Square Garden.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nunes vs Harrison, una pelea histórica por el trono de las MMA femeninas
articles.standfirst: Ambas peleadoras se medirán en el UFC 334 de este sábado con el cinturón de peso gallo en juego
articles.summary: Ambas peleadoras se medirán en el UFC 334 de este sábado con el cinturón de peso gallo en juego
articles.body: Amanda Nunes (23-5) y Kayla Harrison (19-1) protagonizarán este sábado en el UFC 334 -Madison Square Garden, Nueva York- uno de los enfrentamientos más históricos de las MMA femeninas. La peleadora brasileña, considerada la GOAT, ha vuelto tras tres años en el retiro para medirse a la estadounidense, actual campeona y doble medallista de oro olímpica en judo, por lo que este duelo puede determinar quién es la más grande de todos los tiempos a pesar de que Harrison apenas lleva tres combates en la compañía. Nunes es considerada la más grande de todos los tiempos en gran parte porque ha sido doble campeona y ha sido dominante con varias generaciones de peleadoras. Desde su debut en la UFC en 2013, la peleadora brasileña ha sumado 16 victorias y dos derrotas, con diez finalizaciones y 11 victorias en combates titulares. Algunas actuaciones que ha tenido 'The Lioness' la han encumbrado al Olimpo, como sus K.O. en el primer asalto ante Ronda Rousey, Holly Holm y Cris Cyborg, sus dos victorias ante Valentina Shevchenko o su venganza ante Julianna Peña. Sin embargo, decidió dar un paso al lado tras dominar a Irene Aldana porque ya no le quedaban retos por asumir. Ahora que ha visto que Harrison ha entrado en la UFC y ha irrumpido con fuerza, la peleadora brasileña ha vuelto a sentir ese hambre competitiva, y por primera vez desde junio 2023 volverá a subirse al octágono con todas las incógnitas que eso conlleva. De hecho, Nunes ha revelado que a nivel mental necesitaba volver a pelear porque sentía cierto vacío, y si es capaz de vencer a Kayla podría ser entrar en la conversación con Jon Jones o Georges St-Pierre para ser la figura más grande que ha existido en la UFC. Para ello tendrá que vencer a una Kayla Harrison que viene lanzada, ya que desde su debut en abril de 2024 apenas ha necesitado tres combates para ser campeona tras arrasar a Julianna Peña. De hecho, este enfrentamiento iba a darse en enero de este mismo año, pero una grave lesión en el cuello de la estadounidense obligó a la UFC a posponerlo. Harrison ya era campeona de peso ligero en PFL e incluso ganó en dos ocasiones el torneo del millón de dólares, pero en la UFC está teniendo que competir en peso gallo y eso es un gran hándicap por la cantidad de peso que tiene que cortar. De hecho, en los pesajes de esta mañana se ha vuelto a ver a una Kayla muy debilitada, y ha dejado caer que este combate podría ser el último de su carrera profesional. A sus 36 años, Harrison tiene muy poco que demostrar como artista marcial, y en caso de vencer a Nunes ya tendría pocos retos pendientes. De hecho, se podría debatir si es la más grande de todos los tiempos con otra actuación dominante, por lo que sería el escenario perfecto para decir adiós. Es más, existe el posible escenario en el que ambas decidan poner fin definitivamente a su carrera en una velada histórica.

articles.title: UFC: Eight face jail over Usman Nurmagomedov-Merab Dvalishvili mass brawl
articles.summary: Eight people face prison sentences for their part in mass brawl involving MMA fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili at a hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Eight people have received prison sentences for their part in a mass brawl involving MMA fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili at a hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.

A video of the incident appeared to show Russian Nurmagomedov slapping former UFC bantamweight champion Dvalishvili after approaching the Georgian from behind.

Fighting then broke out between the two and members of their teams, with Abu Dhabi police later confirming the incident led to 10 arrests being made.

According to a social media post by Abu Dhabi's judicial department, all 10 defendants have been convicted for their part in the brawl.

A report by Abu Dhabi news outlet the National , external went into more detail, adding that six of the defendants were sentenced to six months in prison, fined £62,000 each and ordered to be deported after completing their sentences.

It added they have been convicted for "disturbing public security, causing panic and endangering lives".

Two others were given the same punishment, but for "violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl".

The remaining two defendants were fined £10,200 each for "disturbing public security and assaulting others".

None of the defendants have yet been named, but Real American Freestyle (RAF) co-founder Chad Bronstein says Dvalishvili has been released from custody.

"I'm pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi," Bronstein said in a statement.

"We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support.

"We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us."

BBC Sport has asked Abu Dhabi's judicial department for confirmation.

Dvalishvili, 35, was scheduled to compete at the RAF event in the United Arab Emirates on Saturday against Brazilian Marlon Moraes.

Dvalishvili released a video after the incident calling Nurmagomedov, 28, and his team "snakes" as he received treatment on his bloodied face.

Nurmagomedov is in Abu Dhabi to support his brother Umar, who was set to compete against American Urijah Faber at Saturday's event.

Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili's teams had a previous altercation at a RAF event in July, which UFC champion Islam Makhachev - a close friend and training partner of the Nurmagomedovs - suggested led to Wednesday's brawl.

Nurmagomedov is the PFL lightweight champion but is out of contract after winning his last bout with the organisation in July.

He has been heavily linked with a switch to the UFC but on Friday the promotion's president Dana White said he had not spoken to the Russian.

White then called the altercation "ridiculous" and "stupid", and referred to the participants as "a bunch of idiots".
