articles.title: Saba Lazishvili, Merab Dvalishvili's friend, snatches Umar Nurmagomedov's RAF match after hotel attack
articles.summary: Saba Lazishvili is going from a hotel brawl to the wrestling mats after an eventful week in Abu Dhabi.
articles.body:
Saba Lazishvili is going from a hotel brawl to the wrestling mats.

The 21-year-old Georgian wrestler, who was involved in Wednesday's violent altercation alongside former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and Usman Nurmagomedov's entourage, has been added to Saturday's RAF Abu Dhabi card at Etihad Arena in the United Arab Emirates .

Lazishvili will replace Umar Nurmagomedov — the older brother of Usman Nurmagomedov — in a freestyle wrestling match against UFC Hall of Famer Urijah Faber, jumping into the event on less than a day's notice.

Lazishvili and Dvalishvili were victims of a brutal group attack Wednesday in a hotel lobby in Abu Dhabi, led by Usman Nurmagomedov. Video of the incident showed Nurmagomedov approaching Dvalishvili then abruptly striking him in the face, igniting a mass brawl in which Lazishvili and Dvalishvili were vastly outnumbered .

Video of the incident's aftermath showed both Lazishvili and Dvalishvili with visible bruising all over their faces, and Dvalishvili badly bloodied.

Abu Dhabi authorities detained multiple individuals following the incident, including Dvalishvili and Lazishvili, who have since been released .

In total, Usman Nurmagomedov was one of eight defendants to receive a six-month sentence, a fine of 300,000 UAE Dirhams (approximately $81,688) and deportation from the country following their stays behind bars.

"It's absolutely ridiculous and stupid and they're all in jail," White said at UFC 334's pre-fight press conference in New York City. "That is not a place to go f*** around."

Despite the incident and his subsequent detention, Dvalishvili is still expected to compete Saturday at RAF Abu Dhabi against former UFC bantamweight contender Marlon Moraes.

And now Lazishvili will make his professional freestyle wrestling debut on the card as well, capping off an eventful week for the new Georgian cult hero.

articles.title: Viddal Riley determined to prove himself a world champion in waiting in European title fight against Seydi Coupe
articles.summary: Viddal Riley puts the European title on the line against Seydi Coupe on Saturday; "I won't be disappointed if I don't stop him. I'll be disappointed if I don't batter him," Riley said; Victory should see Riley closing in on a world title shot
articles.body:
Only 14 fights into his pro career, Riley is already rated as the IBF's No. 2 contender for their world championship.

The Londoner wants to showcase himself as a world champion in waiting against Coupe.

"I think I'm the most well-rounded cruiserweight in the world," Riley told Sky Sports .

"I think we've trained for that because we want to cover every aspect of the game. We don't want to be lacking any area when it comes to movement, speed, IQ. All these things, I have them."

The IBF belt is currently vacant with Riley and New Zealand's David Nyika ranked one and two. Sooner or later a world title fight would surely lie ahead of Riley, if he's victorious.

"He's in the way. We can't worry about the other side of the door until we get past the doorman," Riley said of Coupe.

"I'm trying to get in the club, Seydi's asking for my ID at the door, I have to show him my ID or pull him out the way and get into the club."

It's a fight Riley is determined to dominate.

"I believe this will be a stoppage victory," the Londoner said. "You can't stop everybody, I'm aware of that as well. I won't be disappointed per se if I don't stop him. I'll be disappointed if I don't batter him.

"I just want to show for 12 rounds at least, it's not the level. We're completely different levels and I do, contrary to belief, possess good punch power."

articles.title: Ciryl Gane, el campeón más cuestionado, defiende por primera vez su título en el UFC 334
articles.standfirst: El peleador francés, en el ojo de la polémica por sus golpes ilegales, defenderá en el UFC 334 de este sábado su cinturón de peso pesado ante Josh Hokit
articles.summary: El peleador francés, en el ojo de la polémica por sus golpes ilegales, defenderá en el UFC 334 de este sábado su cinturón de peso pesado ante Josh Hokit
articles.body: Este sábado 14 de noviembre, Ciryl Gane (14-2, 1NC) tendrá la oportunidad de demostrar al mundo de las MMA que es un campeón legítimo al enfrentarse a Josh Hokit (10-0) en el combate estelar del UFC 334, en lo que será su primera defensa de título en peso pesado. El peleador francés ha estado en el ojo de la polémica desde hace un tiempo por algunos resultados dudosos y acciones que para muchos fueron ilegales, y ahora le tocará medirse ante el peleador más polémico de la categoría para disminuir el hate que hay sobre su figura. 'Bon Gamin' llegó a la UFC en 2019, y desde su debut ha demostrado ser uno de los peleadores más atléticos de toda la promotora. Es un peso pesado natural, con un striking muy técnico que es capaz de desarbolar el estilo de sus rivales de diferentes maneras. En apenas dos años, Gane firmó una racha invicta de seis victorias, aunque en una de ellas ante Junior Dos Santos ya protagonizó un K.O. muy polémico por lo que muchos consideraron que fue un codazo en la nuca. Estos resultados le permitieron pelear por el cinturón interino ante Derrick Lewis, al que noqueó en el tercer asalto, pero en la unificación de cinturones ante Francis Ngannou sufrió su primera derrota profesional. Ciryl ganó los dos primeros asaltos en el striking ante uno de los pegadores más temibles de la historia, pero el camerunés mostró su falta de habilidad en la lucha y le remontó la pelea. Poco tiempo más tarde se redimió noqueando a Tai Tuivasa en un duelo en el que estuvo a punto de ser finalizado, pero de nuevo volvió a dar algún que otro golpe en la nuca de su rival. Comenzaba a ser reincidente. Ngannou se fue por la puerta de atrás después de un conflicto con la UFC, y la compañía anunció el regreso de Jon Jones para medirse a Gane e intentar convertirse en doble campeón. A pesar de que algunos creían que el francés podría plantar cara, el GOAT de la UFC hizo con él lo que quiso en el suelo, y le sometió en el primer asalto para volver a dejarle sin cinturón indiscutido. Lejos de venirse abajo, el peleador francés se volvió a reponer finalizando a Serghei Spivac, y a partir de ahí no ha hecho más que protagonizar polémica tras polémica. La primera llegó en su revancha ante Alexander Volkov, ya que venció por decisión dividida un combate en el que muchos le daban como perdedor, incluido el propio Dana White -jefe de la UFC-. Sin embargo, este victoria le permitió pelear por el cinturón ante Tom Aspinall una vez Jon Jones decidió retirarse de manera inesperada. Todo el mundo esperaba un combatazo, pero en el primer asalto 'Bon Gamin' realizó un feo doble piquete de ojos al inglés que le impidió continuar. El resultado fue un 'No Contest' -sin resultado-, y las redes se llenaron de críticas hacia Ciryl. Lejos de ser castigado, y ante la grave lesión de Aspinall, la UFC enfrentó al francés contra Alex Pereira en el UFC Casa Blanca del pasado 14 de junio por el cinturón interino, y de nuevo se ganó más enemigos. 'Bon Gamin' noqueó a 'Poatan' en el segundo asalto, pero las imágenes mostraron como le daba varios golpes en la nuca. A pesar de que Pereira se quejó de ello, Herb Dean -árbitro del combate- decidió no penalizarlo, pero el público sí lo hizo. Desde ese momento, y por mucho que Gane haya intentado justificarse, ha quedado como un peleador sucio, aunque la baja prolongada de Aspinall haya provocado que deje vacante el título e inmediatamente Gane se haya convertido en campeón indiscutido. Eso sí, no de la manera que él deseaba. El propio Hokit se ha burlado de él subiendo vídeos mientras entrenaba cómo defender los piquetes de ojo, o incluso uno en el que le rociaban con gas pimienta para ver cómo superaría una situación similar. De hecho, Josh apareció en la rueda de prensa de ayer con un parche y unas gafas de esquiar, por lo que el beef está servido. Por tanto, este es el momento de Gane de ganar con todas las de la ley y demostrar que es un campeón legítimo.

articles.title: In 2025, Mike Tyson bought a $13 million Florida mansion spanning 12,286 sq ft; the lakefront estate has an 80-foot pool, a gym and a private bass pond
articles.summary: Former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson purchased a $13 million (£11 million) mansion in Delray Beach, Florida, in 2025, following his high-profile
articles.body: Former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson purchased a $13 million (£11 million) mansion in Delray Beach, Florida, in 2025, following his high-profile fight against Jake Paul. articles.title: UFC boss Dana White brushes off Democratic probe threats, recalls 'crazy 48 hours' around Trump job offer
articles.summary: UFC CEO Dana White told Lara Trump he has nothing to hide from post-midterm Democratic probes and recounted his "crazy 48 hours" around President Donald Trump's press secretary joke.
articles.body: UFC CEO Dana White dismissed concerns about a potential congressional investigation by Democrats, saying he is not worried about being targeted over his close ties to President Donald Trump. In a preview of "My View with Lara Trump," set to air in full on Saturday at 9 p.m. ET, White said he expects Democrats to go after him. "Well, I mean, we kind of expected that," White said when asked by Fox News host Lara Trump if he was worried about being targeted by Democrats. BERNIE SANDERS WARNS DEMOCRATS NOT TO SPEND ALL THEIR TIME INVESTIGATING TRUMP "If you didn't do anything illegal or anything wrong, I don't know why you'd have to be worried. I've never done anything in the political world that would be illegal, where anybody should come after me or anything that we have to hide. I expect it, but no, I'm not worried about it." The exchange comes as Democrats prepare their oversight agenda following the Nov. 3 midterms. Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., the incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, recently warned Trump administration officials and allies to "lawyer up" ahead of potential investigations. White has been an outspoken supporter of President Trump and joined him in the White House briefing room Monday, where he addressed reporters. During the interview, White described the experience as "incredible." JACKSON THOMPSON: DANA WHITE SAYS HE'LL MEET WITH TRUMP AMID CLAIM OF WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY JOB OFFER "No, it was incredible. What an amazing experience. Literally, when I was pulling in the gates of the White House, his assistant called and said, ‘Hey, we're going to take you right down to the press room. He wants you in the house,’" White said. "This is crazy. It was a very unique and crazy 48 hours for me." President Trump posted Nov. 7 on Truth Social that he had offered White the White House press secretary position following Katie Zacharia's departure, prompting some questions. "I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," the commander in chief wrote in the post. "Dana, please take the job!" TRUMP'S NEW PRESS SECRETARY OUT OF THE JOB JUST DAYS AFTER ROCKY DEBUT TRUMP CLOSING IN ON NEW PRESS SECRETARY AS ADMINISTRATION OFFICIALS PUSH FOR PICK WHO COULD BREAK THE MOLD Both President Trump and White addressed the post during Monday's briefing, and the president explained he was only joking. "We were having a very bad press day, and I said, 'I don't know why I thought of his name.' He's been my friend for a long time. I said, 'You know, I think I'm going to get Dana White to be my new press secretary,'" President Trump told reporters. "I said it to a group of the press, and that was it. I was sort of kidding, and then they wrote the story as though I wasn't kidding." "I have zero political aspirations," White said. "I was at a fight for Zuffa Boxing in London when he called me and told me that he had done this, and the last 24 hours of my life have been insane." White’s ties to President Trump have drawn attention in recent years, with White speaking at the past three Republican National Conventions. He also partnered with the White House to stage UFC Freedom 250 on the South Lawn, described as the first professional sporting event ever held at the presidential residence. DANA WHITE SAYS 'I DON'T GIVE A S---' IF TRUMP FRIENDSHIP COSTS HIM BUSINESS, 250TH EVENT WAS TRUMP'S IDEA CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital’s Louis Casiano contributed to this report. To watch Fox News host Lara Trump's full interview with UFC CEO Dana White, tune in Saturday at 9 p.m. ET to 'My View with Lara Trump.'

articles.title: Youth Olympics: In Dakar, Ambekar and Gunjan herald a new boxing dawn
articles.summary: KOLKATA: When the final bell rang in Dakar on Thursday, it probably marked a breakthrough moment for Indian sport.
articles.body: KOLKATA: When the final bell rang in Dakar on Thursday, it probably marked a breakthrough moment for Indian sport.In a historic Youth Olympics campaign that yielded 10 medals for India from 17 athletes, boxing provided the brightest spark as Ambekar Meetei claimed India’s first-ever gold medal in the sport, an achievement that was soon followed by Gunjan to complete a remarkable double.For Ambekar, however, the magnitude of the achievement was still sinking in.“It still feels like a dream. I want to thank my family, my coaches and everyone in India who supported me. This medal is for my country,” said the Manipur boxer after winning the men’s 50kg title.The triumph was far from straightforward. Ambekar lost the opening round on all five judges’ scorecards and suddenly found himself chasing the contest. “I told myself not to panic. My coaches asked me to stay calm, move closer and throw fast combinations. I knew there were still two rounds left, so I decided to give my 100% and fight back,” he recalled.The turning point arrived in the second round when a standing count swung the momentum in his favour. “After losing the first round, that punch gave me a lot of confidence. It put pressure on my opponent and helped me take control,” said Ambekar after being Ireland’s Kristian Jubani.The comeback reflected a quality his coach Vijay Kumar Sharma believes defines the teenager.“Ambekar’s fighting spirit and willpower stood out throughout the tournament. He is tactically excellent and follows instructions inside the ring with remarkable discipline,” Sharma said.“Even after losing the first round, he never lost belief and came back with a strong mindset. That resilience under pressure is what impressed me the most about him.”For Ambekar, who hails from Imphal East, the gold was not only a career-defining victory but also the start of something bigger including a journey towards the Los Angeles Olympics.If Ambekar opened the golden chapter, Gunjan ensured it ended on an equally historic note. The youngster became India’s first female Youth Olympic boxing gold medallist.Like Ambekar, her success was built on preparation and composure. “Before the final, I was focused on my game plan. I knew exactly how I wanted to box and what I needed to do inside the ring. My main aim was to have belief in myself and remain confident,” said Gunjan, who won the women’s 48kg title with a victory over Algeria’s Bouthaina Bensalah.For Gunjan, the achievement carried significance beyond the medal itself. “It is a special moment for me and for the country. Winning this gold medal and creating history for India is a dream come true.”Their victories formed the centrepiece of India’s most successful Youth Olympic boxing campaign, contributing to a 10-medal haul that included two gold, three silver and five bronze medals.More importantly, Ambekar and Gunjan delivered something numbers cannot fully capture. In Dakar, they showed that Indian boxing’s next generation is no longer merely dreaming of the Olympic podium. It is already climbing onto it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Not-Retiring Gable Returns At UFC 336
articles.summary: Former Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson isn’t giving up on his fighting dreams. Just a couple months ago, Steveson was shockingly knocked out in just 12...
articles.body:
Former Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson isn't giving up on his fighting dreams .

Just a couple months ago, Steveson was shockingly knocked out in just 12 seconds by Sean Sharaf (watch it again here) at UFC 331. Steveson was widely considered to be the sport's best prospect, and he brought a Jon Jones co-sign with him into the Octagon. After the stunning loss to an unheralded opponent, fans and pundits alike immediately questioned whether Steveson would ever make the walk again , particularly since Steveson already gave up on pursuing NFL and WWE careers previously … and fleeing the Octagon afterward didn't help his reputation either.

As it turns out, Steveson is showing some grit to make a fairly quick return. Per a first report from Connected MMA , Steveson will return to action opposite Terrance Chatman at UFC 336, which is scheduled for Jan. 30, 2027 inside the Scotiabank Arena in Toronto, Ontario, Canada.

Who is Terrance Chatman? The 5-2 Heavyweight made his promotional debut back in August, quickly getting smoked by another top up-and-comer in Anthony Wint (see that finish here) . For further context, Chatman has defeated exactly one opponent with a winning record.

At the same time, Steveson is returning less than six months after a bad knockout. That's always a gamble, and there's a high probability that Chatman is throwing haymakers from the first bell.

articles.title: Ciryl Gane still hopes for Tom Aspinall rematch: 'First fight was not good for him, for me, for everyone'
articles.summary: Ciryl Gane's 2025 fight with Tom Aspinall ended as a no contest due to an eye poke; With Aspinall unable to fight while recovering from the injury, Gane has become the UFC heavyweight champion; But he still hopes to rematch Aspinall
articles.body:
Aspinall's UFC heavyweight title fight with Gane ended in a no contest after the Briton suffered an eye poke.

Unable to compete due to the injury, Aspinall vacated the title . Gane, who won an interim title when he beat Alex Perreira, was elevated to full champion and defends the belt against Josh Hokit at Madison Square Garden on Saturday.

Victory could lead to an eventual rematch with Aspinall. "I hope to. Unfortunately the outcome of this [first] fight was not a good way for me, for him, for everyone. So I hope he's got a bit better from his injury. But it's important for him to recover first," Gane told Sky Sports .

"It was a great first round for me, I think. But it was just the first round so we don't know exactly what's going to happen for the rest of the fight. So it was a really interesting fight, it's really hard to predict… But I started very well."

Aspinall has criticised Gane, calling him a "cheater". The Frenchman responded: "I was a little bit disappointed but he tries to protect himself maybe with this strategy. But unfortunately this happens in MMA so I don't understand.

"This is an accident," he added. "I'm not a guy that disrespects fighters, I like to respect everyone."

articles.title: Carlos Adames fights Gerome Warburton as Denzel Bentley targets shot at WBC middleweight world champion next year
articles.summary: Carlos Adames returns to action against Wales' Gerome Warburton in Riyadh on Saturday; London's Denzel Bentley is looking to challenge Adames for the WBC middleweight world title next year; Watch Adames fight Warburton live on Sky Sports Mix from 4pm
articles.body:
Adames is the reigning WBC middleweight world champion but is tuning up for major title fights next year with a non-title bout against Warburton at a 165lb catchweight.

Adames has an impressive track record. Undefeated at middleweight he's taken top-class wins over Sergiy Derevyanchenko, Julian Williams, Terrell Gausha and Austin Williams. He was unfortunate to be held to a draw against Hamzah Sheeraz, too.

Warburton, a former Welsh champion, has not operated at that level, but this fight with Adames offers him a route to the elite end of the division, if he can score an upset.

The Welshman though is coming off back-to-back wins over Nathan Heaney, the former British champion who defeated Denzel Bentley , who went on afterwards to win a world championship.

Bentley, stripped of his WBO title before his recent victory over Shane Mosley Jr , is gunning to become a world champion once again. He will be a close observer of Adames vs Warburton. Bentley is targeting 2027 fights with Adames and IBF titlist Aaron McKenna.

"Early next year, I'm ready to go again," Bentley told Sky Sports . "I'd love another world title shot. McKenna or Adames, seeing as those are the two middleweights who are at this [Zuffa Boxing] stable with us and they are world champions. Those two are my priority."

He does think Adames will win and be in position to fight for his world title in 2027.

"Congrats to Warburton for getting such a massive fight. I know it's not for the title but he's fighting a champion," Bentley said.

"I expect Adames to come through that," he continued. "Warburton's a good boxer, a nice slick boxer but doesn't carry the power to give Adames any respect or stop him in his tracks.

"Adames is going to walk him down and probably get him out of there. I'd rather see Warburton go the distance. He's done well in his career."

But he added: "Adames gets him out of there, pretty early if I'm being honest."

He will be waiting for Adames. "If he's well enough to go into his mandatory early next year, we can fight maybe summer, a little bit after the summer," Bentley said.

"I'll be happy to wait till after the summer, if it's guaranteed [to be] Adames. If it's not, then I'd like to get out early next year. But if it could be him I'd be happy to wait for that."

articles.title: UFC 334: Amanda Nunes out of retirement for new challenge
articles.summary: Amanda Nunes says the prospect of fighting Kayla Harrison and putting women's MMA back in the spotlight convinced her to come out of retirement to fight at UFC 334 on Saturday.
articles.body:
It was always going to take a special challenge to bring Amanda Nunes out of retirement.

The Brazilian left the UFC in 2023 as the most successful women's mixed martial artist of all time, and with a strong claim to be the greatest ever, regardless of gender.

A former featherweight and bantamweight champion, Nunes is the only woman to hold UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously, and the only fighter, male or female, to successfully defend both belts.

During Nunes' remarkable run, she beat some of the greatest names in MMA history, such as Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg and Valentina Shevchenko.

After Nunes was eventually dethroned by Julianna Pena in one of the biggest upsets of all time, she then regained her title in emphatic fashion.

Nunes was so dominant, she ran out of challengers and left the sport feeling like she had completed MMA.

That was until Kayla Harrison came along.

"When Kayla signed with the UFC and I saw the division with some new girls it excited me," said Nunes.

"Because I cleaned both divisions and didn't have anything to do any more. That was when I was sure I wanted to do this again."

American Harrison is a two-time Olympic gold medallist in judo who became a two-time PFL lightweight world champion after transitioning to MMA.

After joining the UFC in 2024, Harrison won the bantamweight title in only her third fight with the promotion.

The contest between 36-year-old Harrison and 38-year-old Nunes is being described by pundits as one of the biggest women's fights in UFC history.

The pair are friends and former team-mates at American Top Team Gym, before Nunes left in 2022.

They were originally set to fight in January, but the fight got postponed after Harrison required neck and spinal surgery.

They will instead compete at UFC 334 at New York's Madison Square Garden on Saturday.

Nunes beams with excitement at the prospect of returning to the octagon to fight Harrison, and she has lost none of her trademark confidence during her three years away from the sport.

"I'm not here today as a challenger, I'm here today as a double champion," said Nunes.

"I needed a break and did it at the right time for my mind, body and soul.

"There's no hate. It's about the challenge Kayla brings and how great this will be for women's MMA. We want to prove who the best girl is in the cage."

UFC boss White does not like Hokit's 'shtick'

UFC 334: Gane v Hokit - all you need to know

Nunes wants to put women back in spotlight

Nunes has won 23 of her 28 fights since her debut in 2008 during a glittering career, with 13 of those victories coming via knockout.

She holds multiple records, including 11 wins in title fights, which is the most for a woman in UFC history alongside Shevchenko.

Such is Nunes' star power, she has headlined multiple large events during her career, including the landmark UFC 200 show in 2016, where she beat Miesha Tate.

She also headlined when she regained the belt off Pena at UFC 277, and in her last bout against Irene Aldana.

Since then however, only one of 43 UFC numbered events have been headlined by women, which was Natalia Silva's win over Wang Cong at UFC 332 in October.

Nunes says part of her return is fuelled by wanting to help women's MMA return to the spotlight.

"I got upset when I left because I wanted to see the division grow. Back in the day, we put in so much work to this division," said Nunes.

"This is my work here, I want to make women's MMA great, I want the UFC proud of us, so when I saw it slowing down I was a little sad and I got the itch. I want to jump back in and bring it back again."

Nunes has been able to spend more time with her partner Nina and her two daughters during her break from the sport, but admits she has "missed being a fighter".

At the age of 38, it remains to be seen if Nunes' powers have waned, but she says she is planning to fight on past the Harrison match "until my body tells me".

Now, with a new challenge in front of her, Nunes gets the chance to add another chapter to her remarkable story.

articles.title: George Francis: Sex-test error meant boxer missed U19 World Championships
articles.summary: George Francis was left “broken” after he was banned from competing at the Under-19 World Championships because his team did not organise a sex verification test to prove he is male.
articles.body:
A teenage English boxer says he was left "broken" after he was banned from competing at the Under-19 World Championships because his team forgot to organise a sex verification test to prove he is male.

George Francis, 18, was due to fight in the 60kg category in Budva, Montenegro last month.

But Francis, from Loughton, Essex, says that he was informed he was ineligible only hours before the draw because of an "administrative oversight" by governing body England Boxing.

"They got me in a room and told me that I couldn't box because they didn't know if I was a boy or a girl, basically," Francis told BBC Sport.

"The explanation was that they couldn't provide a blood sample for me in time. Everyone else was able to provide a blood sample, but they just forgot me.

"Somehow I wasn't on the system. Apparently, there were no qualified doctors in Budva to do it. It's crazy."

A multiple schoolboy and junior national champion, Francis said he had been training "non-stop" for the "dream" of representing England in his first World Championships.

"It was the worst news I've ever had in my life," said Fracis, whose plight was first reported by the Times newspaper.

"I wouldn't wish it on anyone, to be honest. I was just broken. They were speaking to me and I couldn't even really hear. I was devastated. I couldn't really talk. I literally couldn't feel anything. There was a hole left there."

World Boxing introduced mandatory genetic sex testing for female competitors aged 18 and above last year to ensure "the safety of all participants and provide a level playing field", with national federations responsible for ensuring samples were processed.

The move followed a major controversy in the women's boxing competition at the 2024 Olympics in Paris, where fighters Imane Khelif and Lin Yu-ting both won golds, despite being disqualified from the previous year's World Championships for allegedly failing sex eligibility tests conducted by the then governing body, the International Boxing Association.

In January however, World Boxing extended the rules to include male boxers.

"I can't put into words how it just doesn't make sense," said Francis, who has now missed out on the chance of trying to qualify for the Olympics, and is planing to turn professional.

"I feel like there's nothing really left for me as an amateur.

"I turned 18 four days before flying, so it must have been that they hadn't checked their system in time to get me tested. Going forward, there should be someone there making sure it doesn't happen because I don't want any of these mistakes happening to anybody else."

While Francis' father has been contacted by Boxing England since the episode, his son claims the governing body is yet to contact him directly.

"I haven't had one phone call or message from them. I've just been forgotten about. I don't know how that's been allowed," he said.

In a statement, England Boxing said it "acknowledges that an administrative oversight occurred, once the issue became apparent, we worked closely with the competition organisers to explore all appropriate options in accordance with World Boxing's rules and regulations.

"We maintained open communication with George and his family throughout, despite this, a resolution was not possible.

"George remained a valued member of the England team, including representing the squad as flag bearer.

"England Boxing has no greater priority than the health and wellbeing of athletes on its performance pathway and are committed to learning from this experience and strengthening our processes to prevent a recurrence."

World Boxing has been approached for comment.

In 2025, a dozen female fighters across five nations were barred from the World Championships in Liverpool because deadlines for their sex tests were missed.

articles.title: UFC 334, dos cinturones en juego en el regreso al Madison Square Garden
articles.standfirst: Esta madrugada se celebrará una de las carteleras más importantes del año en un lugar emblemático
articles.summary: Esta madrugada se celebrará una de las carteleras más importantes del año en un lugar emblemático
articles.body: Esta misma noche, la UFC regresa como cada año al Madison Square Garden de Nueva York para celebrar el UFC 334, una cartelera histórica donde habrá dos cinturones en juego y una gran cantidad de grandes combates que convierten este evento en uno de los mejores del año. En este lugar emblemático hace diez años Conor McGregor se convirtió en doble campeón, hace dos Jon Jones peleó por última vez y hace uno Islam Makhachev también logró la doble corona, mientras que esta noche se decidirá el nuevo campeón de peso pesado y quién es la verdadera reina de las MMA femeninas. En el combate estelar, Josh Hokit (10-0) y Ciryl Gane (14-2) se medirán en lo que será la primera defensa del cinturón indiscutido de peso pesado para el francés tras el anuncio de que Tom Aspinall dejaba vacante el título seguir arrastrando una lesión ocular de su último enfrentamiento ante 'Bon Gamin' con ese ya famoso doble piquete de ojos. Hokit tiene una oportunidad de oro para dar un golpe sobre la mesa y demostrar que las expectativas que hay puestas en él están justificadas, ya que en caso de finalizar a Gane podría convertirse en toda una superestrella. Por otra parte, en el combate co estelar Amanda Nunes (23-5) y Kayla Harrison (19-1) se enfrentarán por el cinturón de peso gallo femenino. La peleadora brasileña, considerada la GOAT de las MMA femeninas, vuelve del retiro tras tres años inactiva para medirse a una doble medallista de oro olímpico en judo como es Kayla, en lo que puede ser uno de los duelos más históricos de la UFC. Harrison apenas ha necesitado tres combates en la compañía para ser campeona, pero ahora tendrá en frente al reto definitivo. En el resto de la cartelera habrá otros grandes nombres y enfrentamientos a analizar. Por ejemplo, Stephen Thompson (17-9-1) realizará su última pelea profesional antes Charles Radtke (12-5) para poner la guinda del pastel a una gran carrera en peso wélter, donde llegó a pelear por el título y asombró al mundo con su arsenal de patadas. Además, Yousri Belgaroui (11-3) tendrá su primera prueba de fuego en peso medio ante Caio Borralho (18-2, 1NC), donde está ascendiendo a un ritmo vertiginoso de la mano de Alex Pereira y Glover Teixeira. El combate del pueblo será el que enfrente a Uros Medic (14-3) y Kevin Holland (29-15, 1NC), en un duelo que sería extraño que llegase a los puntos teniendo en cuenta que el peleador serbio solo sabe finalizar en el primer asalto y el estadounidense es uno de los mayores 'showman' del peso wélter. Además, Bilal Hasan (10-0, 1NC) se medirá a Luis Gurule (11-4) en peso mosca para intentar finalizarle y demostrar que está destinado a ser una auténtica superestrella en su categoría. A priori, este evento debería ser una oda a las MMA, ya que hay duelo de todo tipo y el espectáculo está asegurado. Hay mucho en juego a lo largo de esta cartelera, y seguramente sea una que se recuerde con mucho cariño con el paso de los años. Cada vez que la UFC aterriza en el Madison Square Garden no deja indiferente a nadie, y en esta ocasión no tiene pinta de que vaya a haber una excepción.

articles.title: Eight sentenced to jail over Nurmagomedov-Dvalishvili Abu Dhabi hotel brawl
articles.summary: A brawl broke out between the two MMA fighters and their teams inside a hotel before a wrestling event.
articles.body:
The Abu Dhabi Criminal Court has convicted 10 people over a mass brawl ⁠involving mixed ⁠martial artists Usman Nurmagomedov, Merab Dvalishvili and their teammates at a hotel.

The brawl broke out ahead of a wrestling event organised ⁠by Real American Freestyle (RAF), where Usman Nurmagomedov’s brother Umar and Dvalishvili were scheduled for matches against different opponents.

“An Abu Dhabi court has convicted 10 defendants in connection with a brawl ‌inside a hotel and has sentenced them to six months’ imprisonment … along with deportation from the country,” read the announcement from the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department on Friday.

ESPN reported that six members of Team Nurmagomedov were sentenced to six months in prison, fined 300,000 dirhams (approximately $81,600) and ordered to be deported after serving their sentences.

According to Abu Dhabi-based The National newspaper, former UFC bantamweight ⁠champion Dvalishvili and a friend were fined 50,000 dirhams ($13,600) for “disturbing public security and assaulting others”.

Two additional people were handed six-month prison sentences for privacy violations after they filmed the ⁠brawl and published the footage online, the reports added. The court also ordered the confiscation of their phones and deletion of the footage.

The brawl broke out on Wednesday when Georgian Dvalishvili, who was scheduled to appear at RAF Abu Dhabi on Saturday, was being interviewed in the lobby of the Yas Hilton.

PFL lightweight champion Usman – the cousin of retired MMA legend Khabib Nurmagomedov – and his associates approached Dvalishvili. Videos shared online showed ‌Usman coming in from behind and slapping Dvalishvili, which started the melee.

Usman was not scheduled to feature at the RAF Abu Dhabi card but travelled to the UAE capital to accompany his older brother, Umar, who was scheduled to face Urijah Faber.

Later on Friday, the event organisers removed Umar from the card, replacing him ‌with ‌Saba Lazishvili, Dvalishvili’s friend who was also involved in the brawl.

RAF cofounder Chad Bronstein said Dvalishvili has been released from custody. He remains available for his scheduled match with Marlon Moraes.

“I’m pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi,” Bronstein said in a statement. “We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support.”

Dvalishvili posted several videos on social media after the incident and released his personal statement on X, saying: “Just want to let everyone know I have been released, and I am good, healthy and ready to go.

“I want to thank everyone in Abu Dhabi for your help in resolving this matter … I do hope that they release everyone; I would not press charges. I want peace and the best for all,” he added.

Wednesday’s incident wasn’t the first time Dvalishvili and Team Nurmagomedov clashed. Tensions also escalated in January last year after Dvalishvili defeated Usman’s older brother Umar in a UFC bantamweight title fight. They also had a smaller altercation at an RAF event in Georgia in July.

articles.body:
IBF champion McKenna will fight unbeaten Latvian Jevgenijs Aleksejevs at The Venue in Riyadh in the main event of Riyadh Season Zuffa Boxing 14.

It will be McKenna's first defence of the world title belt he won by beating Etinosa Oliha on a memorable night in Dublin.

McKenna, 21-0 (10), who hails from Monaghan, Ireland, is a nine-year pro who vaulted into title contention with his April 2025 decision over former world champion Liam Smith.

While McKenna fought many times in Ireland as a top amateur, he returned home for the first time as a pro in August, capturing the world title with a one-sided victory over Oliha at Dublin's 3Arena.

Aleksejevs, a world-ranked contender who has had 10 stoppage victories in his 20 professional wins, will be challenging for a world title for the first time.

A former kickboxing standout, Aleksejevs has been perfect in gloved combat, securing a regional title last October with a unanimous decision over Przemyslaw Zysk. In February, he outlasted Italy's Damiano Falcinelli over 10 tense rounds.

Former European champion and world title challenger Jack Massey returns to action against Andrew Tabiti.

Massey, 23-4 (13), is looking to rebound from a stunning defeat to Chev Clarke on June's Zuffa Boxing 07 bill. He had Clarke on the deck twice in round four before being stopped in the seventh.

America's Tabiti, who fought Yuniel Dorticos for the world title, has been operating at heavyweight and now returns to the cruiserweight division.

London's Chelli is coming off a stunning upset knockout victory over David Morrell.

Rising welterweight prospect Alex "The Villain" MacMillan, 5-0 (4), returns against an opponent to be named in a six-rounder.

In a preliminary bout, former heavyweight titlist and Anthony Joshua opponent, "Prince" Charles Martin will fight Vladyslav Sirenko, the dangerous Ukrainian with a 23-1 (20) record, who is fresh off his knockout win over Otto Wallin in July.

articles.title: Tommy McMillen, la 'nueva' estrella de UFC: supuesta sobredosis y vuelta a los entrenamientos mientras pide pelear
articles.standfirst: Según varios medios, el compañero de gimnasio de Sean O'Malley sufrió un desagradable episodio durante una fiesta, pero ya está de vuelta en el gimnasio
articles.summary: Según varios medios, el compañero de gimnasio de Sean O'Malley sufrió un desagradable episodio durante una fiesta, pero ya está de vuelta en el gimnasio
articles.body: La vida de Tommy McMillen ha dado un vuelco en el último año. Desde que entrase en la UFC en 2025 a través de las Dana White's Contender Series, el compañero de equipo de Sean O'Malley ha sumado este año tres victorias, dos finalizaciones y tres bonos de la noche, lo que le han convertido en una superestrella. Sin embargo, también se ha caracterizado por ser un personaje díscolo fuera del octágono, y según han reportado varios medios hace unos días sufrió una supuesta sobredosis durante una fiesta y se le encontraron inconsciente. Eso sí, 'Gun' ha vuelto a las redes y ha afirmado que está disponible para una llamada en corto aviso para pelear. McMillen siempre ha dicho que lleva una vida más propia del GTA a nivel privado. Ha reconocido que ha llegado a estar de fiesta tres días, es un gangster y farda de ello cada vez que puede. Eso sí, esta vez ha excedido ciertos límites, ya que según informó TMZ tuvo que ser trasladado al hospital de Arizona hace unos días tras ser encontrado inconsciente en el baño de una discoteca. De hecho, los agentes presentes en la escena le tuvieron que administrar Narcan al encontrar una sustancia blanca cerca de él. Un susto muy serio del que ha salido ileso afortunadamente, ya que pocas horas después el propio McMillen se manifestó en redes sociales mencionando a la UFC y dejando un mensaje muy claro. "Listo para una llamada en corto aviso". Es más, ya se ha vuelto a ver a Tommy entrenando y parece preparado para seguir su ascenso en la división de peso pluma de la UFC. Uno de los primeros en pronunciarse al respecto fue Tim Welch, entrenador de McMillen y O'Malley, que aseguró que "Tommy está bien y ya está entrenando". Eso sí, en ningún momento ha negado el suceso, por lo que todo hace indicar que fue cierto y McMillen estuvo al borde de tener un susto aún mayor. El que también ha opinado sobre el estilo de vida de McMillen es Sean O'Malley en una entrevista con Ariel Helwani, donde ha afirmado que “no estoy muy preocupado por él. Sé que va a concentrarse al máximo... Punto pivotal en su carrera. Podría ir por aquí, o por allá. La elección es suya, y al final tiene que tomarla". Es difícil pensar en un McMillen sin desfasar y salir de fiesta, pero la realidad es que cada vez se tendrá que enfrentar a retos más difíciles en la división de peso pluma, donde ya está cerca del top 15, así que deberá centrarse si no quiere que su tren descarrile antes de lo previsto.

articles.title: Carlos Adames slams Gerome Warburton after 10-round domination: 'He could have done more, but he was just surviving'
articles.summary: WBC middleweight champion Carlos Adames is a class above Gerome Warburton, winning a wide unanimous decision in their 10-round non-title bout in Riyadh; Watch Aaron McKenna vs Jevgenijs Aleksejevs on Friday December 4 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
They were boxing over 10 rounds in a non-title bout at a catchweight of 165lbs, but for the unheralded Warburton it was a step up into a whole new class.

The Briton seemed almost surprised that he managed to go deep into the fight and celebrated going the distance at the end of their fight in Riyadh.

Adames began tamely himself, restrained in his offensive output but Warburton did even less.

The Welsh southpaw backpedalled as Adames trudged forward and looked to land single shots.

After three quiet rounds, Adames brought in more pressure, forcing Warburton towards the ropes. The Briton grew busier with his jab but Adames was hunting him down.

In the fifth round, Adames sank his right into body, cracked the backhand to head and started to crank up pressure.

Punches strayed to the beltline but Adames was the aggressor throughout as he worked Warburton over.

He attacked in the final round but had left his charge too late and took a unanimous decision win, 100-90, 99-91 and 98-92 on the scorecards.

"I think he was just in the ring to survive, he wasn't really here to win the fight," Adames said. "I think he could have done more, but I think he was just surviving.

" Who wants to fight Carlos Adames? " he declared. "Anybody, 160-168lbs, anybody can get it."

Former world champion Jason Moloney took a clear unanimous decision win over Mexico's Andres Teran in their bantamweight 10 rounder.

Teran, coming off a good stoppage win over previously unbeaten prospect Floyd Diaz, worked to close down Moloney.

But the Australian dashed in a left hook and plunged his right over the top, bounding in and out.

Teran traded solid punches with him and Moloney felt a wide right, swung in to counter one of his attacks, though he regrouped.

Breathing heavily at the halfway point, Moloney still darted in with a right uppercut and worked a left hook into Teran's body. But the Mexican took the hits well.

Moloney's corner instructed him to ease off the power in his punches but his jab still pinged in. He slammed in a right hook and moved out.

In the ninth round, Moloney banged a flush cross into Teran's jaw. He set up a strong left hook too. Jabbing, Moloney shifted in and out on his feet and planted another backhand shot over the Mexican's left arm. Teran was left swinging wildly for his opponent.

Moloney controlled the last round and won 99-91, 98-92 and 97-93 on the scorecards.

French super-middleweight contender Bruno Surace beat Polish southpaw Kamil Bednarek on a unanimous decision.

articles.body: Carlos Adames may still be the best middleweight in the world, but anyone watching Zuffa Boxing 13 on Saturday may not have left entirely convinced.Adames routed the overmatched Gerome Warburton for an uninspiring unanimous decision win (100-90, 99-91, 98-92) in their 10-round main event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.Adames (26-1-1, 18 KOs), making his Zuffa Boxing debut, is the WBC middleweight champion, but his title was not on the line for Saturday's 165-pound catchweight contest. The WBC ordered Adames to fight a pair of mandatory challengers, Meiirim Nursultanov and Jesus Ramos Jr., at its convention earlier this week. If Adames continues to campaign at 160 pounds, Nursultanov and Ramos will likely be his next opponents.The pride of the Dominican Republic 🤩🇩🇴 @BroncoAdames takes the UD victory at Riyadh Season #ZuffaBoxing13 💥@RiyadhSeason | #RiyadhSeason pic.twitter.com/F59h60INV2— Zuffa_Boxing (@Zuffa_Boxing) November 14, 2026 Warburton (18-3-2, 4 KOs) entered Saturday's contest on a three-fight win streak but had previously suffered two defeats and two draws in his pro career, all against opposition well below the world level. Most recently, Kieron Conway stopped Warburton in four rounds in their British title fight in May 2025. Thus, Adames was expected to blast out Warburton early and look impressive — but he wasn't able to deliver that kind of performance.Instead, Adames struggled to pin down Warburton and land any meaningful punches on the British fighter. articles.title: World champion Adames beats Welshman Warburton by unanimous decision
articles.summary: WBC middleweight champion Carlos Adames beats Gerome Warburton by unanimous decision in a non-title super middleweight bout.
articles.body:
WBC middleweight champion Carlos Adames beat Gerome Warburton by unanimous decision in a non-title super middleweight bout in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

Warburton, who holds the WBC continental title, climbed the ropes in the corner after the final round to celebrate going the distance against top-ranked Adames.

The Welshman raised his gloves in pride, but surely knew the referee would raise Adames' hand, with all three judges scoring the fight in the Dominican's favour (100-90, 98-92, 99-91).

Adames, who was making his Zuffa Boxing debut, dominated the fight from the first bell until the last as Warburton, now 18-2-3 as a professional, adopted a defensive approach.

It served the Colwyn Bay fighter well as he withstood some strong shots from Adames, who now boasts a 26-1-1 professional record.

Most of Adames success came with shots to the body, but he never threatened to claim a 19th career knockout victory against an opponent who showed flashes of danger.

Having stayed in the fight, Warburton's best offence came in the later rounds, with the eighth and 10th being awarded to him by one of the judges.
